The '''Duck''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack|image=Puppy Icon.png}}'''. When sold, it will increase the health of all pets currently in the shop. When levelled up, the amount of health given is increased. This health buff will not apply to future animals if the shop is rolled.

== Strategy ==

Duck is in contention for the strongest tier 1 in Turtle Pack, if not the entire game. It has a fantastic base statline that will often win or tie the fight on turn 1, and the health it gives is powerful in the early and midgame as a starting point for buffing important pets. Duck can very often be positioned to buff 3-4 relevant targets, an effective +3 or +4 buff!

The most important way to get full value out of Duck involves playing slightly differently than usual. On turn 3, you will often have 3 copies to combine for a tier up reward. With Duck, it's important to roll before levelling up any pets on your board. Once you find a shop with some good tier 2 buff targets, such as {{IconSAP|Swan}}, {{IconSAP|Peacock}} or {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}}, then you can take your level ups. This will add the tier 3 pets to the shop alongside the tier 2s, and you can then sell your Duck(s) onto everything!

A common mistake that people will make with duck is trying to hold onto it for too long - the stats duck provides are not only good in the long term for additional stats, but are amazing tempo, especially on pets like Peacock, Kangaroo and {{IconSAP|Camel}}. You should always be trying to sell Duck onto a mixture of tier 2 and 3 pets on turn 3!

== Trivia ==
*The Duck's standard sprite depicts a male Mallard Duck with its legs tucked in, suggesting that it is in a sitting or floating position.

|level_2= Sell: Give two random friends +2 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}}.
|level_3= Sell: Give two random friends +3 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}}.
}}

The '''Beaver''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack|image=Puppy Icon.png}}'''. When the Beaver is sold, it will give buff the attack of 2 friends. The friends buffed by the Beaver are chosen at random; however, the same friend will never be buffed twice. If there is only one friend left after selling the Beaver, it will buff the remaining friend only once. Levelling up the Beaver increases the amount of attack given to each of the 2 friends. 

== Strategy ==
The strength of the Beaver lies within its ability to scale by being sold, providing 2 points of permanent attack and an early 3/2 stat-line for the net cost of 2 gold.  While not having an ability that benefits combat, the Beaver is relatively viable round one option due it's high attack allowing it to trade with pets with the 2/3 base stats as well as it's relative safety regarding {{IconSAP|Mosquito}} or {{IconSAP|Tennis Ball}} snipes compared to something like the {{IconSAP|Pig}}. 

Early Tier 1 pets that are intended to be kept for a long time will highly benefit from being paired with the Beavers early scaling, as their abilities are far more relevant in the mid and late game compared to other tier 1 pets.  

Pets that provide benefits from being sold aren't super compatible with the Beaver, as they don't benefit from the permanent attack bonus the Beaver provides. An early example of this is the {{IconSAP|Otter}} as its permanent Health bonus to a random pet would not benefit a Beaver that benefits from being sold. This can be avoided by purchasing the Otter before purchasing the Beaver. 

Beaver is fantastic in conjunction with {{IconSAP|Duck}}, evening out the statlines of pets that were buffed by your duck. Beaver gives a fantastic edge to pets that benefit from attack, and allow them to get off the ground faster - in {{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}, this typically means {{IconSAP|Ox}}, {{IconSAP|Badger}} and {{IconSAP|Dodo}}

Apart from the early game, the Beaver highly benefits the [[Buy-sell Pets|Buy/Sell]] archetype. Pets such as the {{IconSAP|Dragon}}, {{IconSAP|Buffalo}} and {{IconSAP|Shrimp}} benefit from the Beaver as it being sold enables their abilities, as well as providing 2 extra points of permanent attack across the team.

}}

The '''Pigeon''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Selling Pigeon stocks a free {{IconSAP|Bread Crumbs}} in the shop, which when bought will give +1 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}} to a pet. Leveling up the Pigeon increases the amount of Bread Crumbs stocked when Pigeon is sold.

==Strategy==
At first glance, it might seem like a worse {{IconSAP|Beaver}} that gives weaker buff. However what's unique about Pigeon is that the Bread Crumbs are ''targeted'' buffs instead of random, can be frozen to be used on later turns, accumulate in the shop, and provide synergies with food pets.

Pigeon's most notable combo is with {{IconSAP|Rabbit}}, which can be found as early as turn 3. With a Rabbit on the team, each Bread Crumbs acts as a free +1/+1 buff. Buy-selling Pigeon can also be worth it as 2 gold for the same amount of stats as an {{IconSAP|Apple}}.

A common strategy is leveling up Pigeons on turn 3 to try to spawn Rabbit, selling the level 2 Pigeon, buying the Rabbit and then the 2 Bread Crumbs for a +2/+2 buff.

The '''Otter''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When bought, the Otter will increase the stats of a random friend by +1 health. Levelling up the Otter will increase the amount of friends that it gives the +1 health buff to.

Like all Buy pets, the Otter's ability will also activate when an Otter from the shop is merged with an existing Otter, which is the only way to activate the Level 2 and Level 3 effects. If there is only one other pet on the team and the Otter's level 2 or 3 ability is triggered it will still only buff the pet for 1 health once and the extra stats will go to waste. 

==Strategy==

Sadly, Otter is quite bad compared to the other stat-boosting pets in {{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}} {{IconSAP|Tier 1}}. 3 gold for 1 health (only 2 gold if you buy-sell it) is very inefficient compared to {{IconSAP|Beaver}} or {{IconSAP|Duck}} or even {{IconSAP|Apple}}, 3 gold for double the stats of an Otter. On top of this, its mediocre 1/3 statline often loses in the early game, losing 1v1 to 3/2 and 2/3 pets. 

If you see a pair of Otters on turn 1, they are still viable! Using Otter to buff Otter is often its best niche, as a self-scaling buff target, a potential level 2 to be buffed by {{IconSAP|Penguin}} or a potential level 3 to buff {{IconSAP|Bison}}. In either case, the additional stats that the Otter provides itself need to do a lot of heavy lifting to make up for its lack of an ability and weakness to {{IconSAP|Rhino}} !

}}
The '''Pig''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When sold it will grant the player extra {{IconSAP|Gold}} ''(referring to the piggy bank). Levelling up the Pig increases the amount of gold granted upon being sold.

Selling a level 1 pig will reward you with 1 gold for the pet, and 1 extra from the ability, but a level 2 pet will sell for 4 gold because it is level 2, but 2 extra from the ability, and in the same way, selling a level 3 pet will give you 6 gold in total.

==Strategy==

The Pig is a great example of how the value of your gold increases as your run progresses. If you're able to, levelling up a Pig to level 2 can enable you to hold onto the solid 6/3 body for multiple turns, and sell it to use the gold on higher tier, more powerful pets. Typically you want to save level 2 Pig for an odd turn, like turn 5 or 7, since the new shop tier has just unlocked and the pig gold can now find far more valuable units than it could last turn. 

Thus, Pig is a strong pivoting tool that allows you to bring less useful gold into the future, while still getting value out of its chaotic statline that can often clear the way for one of your bigger pets to sweep through a fight!

The '''Ant''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When the Ant [[Faint (Trigger)|faints]], it buffs the stats of one random friend. Levelling up the Ant increases the stats given by its ability.
==Strategy==
The Ant's stats are mid, but its ability is good for a Tier 1 Pet. Not only does the Ant's good attack mean it can trade with most tier 1 pets, but its buff when fainting often allows one of its friends to get an extra KO, meaning the Ant often trades 2-for-1. 

However, this doesn't always pan out in practice. Firstly, if the Ant's buff hits a 1 health friend, then that friend is unlikely to get an extra KO, wasting the Ant's ability. Secondly, it can't trade with a {{IconSAP|Duck}}, {{IconSAP|Marmoset}} or {{IconSAP|Seahorse}}. Having multiple Ants will simply multiply these weaknesses, so it's usually better not to have multiple Ants in the first round.

As most Tier 1 pets do, the Ant falls off in the mid-game. Though the Ant still has power in that it can be given a {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}}, its ability will activate and give one of its friends a nice, permanent buff to their stats. 

Overall, the Ant is a very powerful early game unit that can easily win early rounds, and can be sacrificed for scaling later on.

The Ant is the opposite of the {{IconSAP|Strawberry}} but buffs the back-most friend instead of a random friend.

The '''Mosquito''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. It has subpar stats, and at the start of battle, the Mosquito will deal 1 damage to a random enemy. Levelling up the Mosquito will increase the amount of enemies its ability will target.


==Strategy==
The Mosquito feels mediocre, and only takable if you have atleast 2 or 3 copies of it in the shop during your first turn. It provides the same amount of tempo (value during the turn it is played) as {{IconSAP|Duck}}, {{IconSAP|Beaver}}, and {{IconSAP|Fish}}, except that unlike them, the Mosquito provides no benefit mid-game, and has a possible negative effect of it being able hit Hurt ability pets like {{IconSAP|Peacock}}, more often in versus.

The Mosquito can pop {{IconSAP|Melon}} and harm other cases of perks that reduce damage a limited amount of times. While that is true, it happens lategame. You run the risk of putting it in mid-game, with it being underpowered there. Also, there's better means of popping Melons, such as {{IconSAP|Rhino}}, or simply putting a weak unit up-front.

The '''Fish''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Upon levelling up the Fish will give 2 random friends a buff to their stats. Levelling up the Fish increases the amount of stats given. 

==Strategy==
The Fish is a reasonably solid pet in the early game. 

While it may seem like a good idea to level up the Fish into a pet of the next tier on turns 3, 5, 7 and 9, doing this with another pet would be better because then the next tier pet that you buy can then receive the buff from the Fish once you do end up leveling it.

The Fish is a good candidate for getting to level 3 so that it may enable a {{IconSAP|Bison}}, as levelling it up will scale your team while you're waiting for it to become available.

Getting at least 3 Fish within the first 5 or so turns of a game can be of great help in scaling pets that you want to take into the later stages of the game. This is especially true for {{IconSAP|Jellyfish}} that benefits twice as much from a fish level up at level one. Other synergies include in battle level ups from {{IconSAP|Pug}} and {{IconSAP|Blobfish}} that will provide a temporary buff for the rest of the team if the Fish is placed near the front.

==Trivia==
Fish and {{IconSAP|Lucky Cat}} are only the pets that doesn't have an ability when level 3

fish cant activate its level 1 abillity

The '''Cricket''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Cricket faints, it summons a weak {{IconSAP|Zombie Cricket}} in its place. Levelling up the Cricket increases the stats and level of the summoned Zombie Cricket.

==Strategy==
The Cricket, with low stats and a mediocre ability, can typically be most useful in the early game. It fits best in {{IconSAP|Horse}} teams, as it is the only tier one summoner and can additionally work in front of an early {{IconSAP|Ox}}. Most other synergies are better filled using a more versatile long term summon pet like a {{IconSAP|Deer}} or {{IconSAP|Fly}}.

However, if you are going to be going late-game with the cricket for achievement hunting, the best strategy is to put it in the back. This means that if the cricket ties with the other back pet, it will summon a cricket and get you a win instead of a draw. Leveling the cricket, which is normally a bad idea, can allow the Zombie Cricket to survive a summoned {{IconSAP|Bee}}, another very common tie-breaker.

The '''Horse''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Whenever a friendly pet fills an empty slot, either by buying them or via an ability, Horse will give them a small amount of attack until next turn. Leveling up the Horse increases the amount of attack it gives to summoned friends.

Horse has a hidden interaction: It can be merged with {{IconSAP|Eagle}} to transform into a 5/5 level 1 {{IconSAP|Hippogriff}}.

==Strategy==
Horse strengthens any pet newly added to the team, improves the battle capabilities of summoners such as {{IconSAP|Cricket}}, {{IconSAP|Honey}} perk, {{IconSAP|Spider}}, {{IconSAP|Sheep}}, and can easily dominate the first few turns. Keeping a Horse on the team also makes it easier to pivot later; you don't lose too much stats when selling existing pets since the replacement will receive some attack from Horse, albeit only for one turn.

If you're planning to buy a Horse, it should be bought before other pets so it can give them extra attack for the next battle. When paired with summoners, it should be put behind them to buff the summoned pets in battle. Although, with 1 health at base stats, Horse is very vulnerable to snipers such as {{IconSAP|Mosquito}} and {{IconSAP|Dolphin}} that will knock it out before it can contribute anything to the battle.

For summon teams, you can find a direct upgrade at tier 5: {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, which not only gives more stats but also permanently instead of temporarily. For other scaling focused teams, Horse's ability quickly becomes useless with no targets to give buffs to, and should be replaced ASAP.

'''Snail''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. At the end of turn, if the player lost the last battle, Snail will give the three nearest friends ahead {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}}. Leveling up Snail increases the amount of attack it gives.

Snail's ability will only trigger if the player ''lost'' the last battle, not if it was a draw. This is indicated by a sparkling effect on the Snail while it's in the shop.

If Snail is bought on turn 1, the "last battle" will be considered a draw.

==Strategy==
Snail can be thought of as compensation for losing, or as a passive scaler with a condition. If kept around, Snail can give its buffs for a maximum of 5 times as you progress through the game. It should be placed in the last 2 positions so as to not waste the buffs.

If you lose on turn 2, due to the life regain on turn 3, Snail can trigger the buff without costing a life. Depending on how much you value Snail's buff, you can try to sabotage your team on turn 2 to guarantee Snail trigger.

'''Snail''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. At the end of turn, if the player lost the last battle, Snail will give the three nearest friends ahead {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}}. Leveling up Snail increases the amount of attack it gives.

Snail's ability will only trigger if the player ''lost'' the last battle, not if it was a draw. This is indicated by a sparkling effect on the Snail while it's in the shop.

If Snail is bought on turn 1, the "last battle" will be considered a draw.

==Strategy==
Snail can be thought of as compensation for losing, or as a passive scaler with a condition. If kept around, Snail can give its buffs for a maximum of 5 times as you progress through the game. It should be placed in the last 2 positions so as to not waste the buffs.

If you lose on turn 2, due to the life regain on turn 3, Snail can trigger the buff without costing a life. Depending on how much you value Snail's buff, you can try to sabotage your team on turn 2 to guarantee Snail trigger.

The '''Crab''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. At the start of battle the Crab will gain a percentage of health from the healthiest friend. The percentage of health it gain increases as it levels up.  

==Strategy==
The Crab is a pet that needs to be at level 2 to be viable. Without a level up copying 50% is negligible, especially so in the early game and a waste of gold later on. If you do manage to get it to level 2 or 3 it does a decent job at a serving as a damage sponge that you don't need to put as much effort into scaling. 

On the topic of scaling, it is highly inefficient to scale a crab due to the fact that it's own health value is irrelevant prior to it's ability activating.  

To make up for a likely low attack value, it is recommended to equip the Crab with a {{IconSAP|Meat Bone}} or even a {{IconSAP|Steak}}. It can synergise nicely with a {{IconSAP|Dodo}}, that will increase it's attack in a similar fashion. Using a Dodo + a high Health Pet makes the Crabs stats entirely dependent on other animals, which isn't necessarily bad and actually enables it to be sold without losing many stats or {{IconSAP|Gold}} efficiency.

|level_3='''Faint''': Summon three 1/1 {{IconSAP|Dirty Rat|name=Dirty Rats}} up front for the opponent.

The '''Rat''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Rat faints, it summons a level 1 {{IconSAP|Dirty Rat}} at the front of ''the enemy's team''. Leveling up the Rat will increase the amount of Dirty Rats summoned.

==Strategy==
Rat will summon pets for the enemy, which is almost always a detriment. It's a risky buy that is often only used for its high stats in early turns. You should not overvalue its potential synergies with other pets. Never put Rat in front of {{IconSAP|Ox}}. And '''never''' put Rat in the last position.

With all that said, since Dirty Rats are weak and can be easily knocked out, they can be used to give additional triggers to certain types of ability: '''Hurt''' pets ({{IconSAP|Peacock}}, {{IconSAP|Camel}}), '''Knock out''' pets ({{IconSAP|Hippo}}, {{IconSAP|Rhino}}), and '''After attack''' pets ({{IconSAP|Elephant}}). By putting Rat directly in front of pets with these abilities, it will summon Dirty Rats for the opponent which when attacked will trigger the ability at the cost of only 1 damage per Dirty Rat. These synergies can be further amplified with supporters like {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}}, {{IconSAP|Snake}}, or {{IconSAP|Tiger}} behind the pet that will be facing the Dirty Rats.

Another use for Rat is body blocking the enemy's summons. For example, when Rat trades with a {{IconSAP|Deer}} and they knock each other out, if the Rat has higher attack, the Dirty Rats will be summoned first, blocking the {{IconSAP|Bus}} from being summoned. Though this is rather niche and rarely happens on purpose.

To avoid less or no Dirty Rats being spawned, some enemies must first be knocked out to create space. This often means Rat has to be scaled and act as a tank or else it will waste the ability. Although, not triggering the ability might actually be a positive.

The '''Hedgehog''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When the Hedgehog faints, it deals damage to all pets in play, regardless of whether they are on the player's or the enemy's team. When leveled up, the Hedgehog will deal more damage with its ability. 

==Strategy==
The Hedgehog is the definition of risk-reward. It can deal a LOT of damage to the enemy team, but it can greatly weaken your team, too. It can also serve as an early version of Badger, placed at the back to try and knock out any left over enemies should they have defeated the rest of your team. 

The Hedgehog works best with Pets with Hurt effects, like the {{IconSAP|Blowfish}} and the {{IconSAP|Camel}}. In the '''Puppy Pack''', another notable synergy with the Hedgehog is the {{IconSAP|Microbe}}. Using a {{IconSAP|Skunk}} can help take down the opponent's biggest pet in the late game (since single high health Pets are a big threat to a Hedgehog). In the early game, if you expect both teams to die from your hedgehog, then make sure to include Pets that spawn other units on your team. Ironically, the Hedgehog's biggest weakness is also Pets with Hurt effects. Triggering your opponent's hurt effects for free will most likely result in a loss.

If you plan on using the Hedgehog, make sure to give lots of pets in your team {{IconSAP|Garlic}}, as this can contribute towards negating some of the damage your team takes. Give the Hedgehog itself {{IconSAP|Meat Bone}} and put it in the front. You can use {{IconSAP|Pineapple}} on the hedgehog to greatly increase it's effectiveness, though it is risky. Late game, give it either a {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} or a {{IconSAP|Steak}}. Consider selling the Hedgehog as another late game option, as the 1 {{IconSAP|Gold}} it provides may be more useful than its effect. If you don’t sell it, then in many situations two Hedgehogs are better than one.

The '''Peacock''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Peacock takes damage, it gains attack. Leveling up the Peacock will increase the amount of attack it gains when hurt. 

==Strategy==
The '''Peacock''' is best paired with the {{IconSAP|Elephant}}, which will deal safe amounts of damage and it will be able to gain lots of attack in battle. Though, early on, it might be a good idea to give it {{IconSAP|Honey}}, as it will become a glass cannon.

Like most Pets with [[Hurt Pets|Hurt Abilities]], the Peacock benefits immensely from {{IconSAP|Garlic}} and later on, {{IconSAP|Lemon}} or {{IconSAP|Pita Bread}} due to their damage reductions or health gained when taking damage - something the Peacock wants to do while still being able to stay alive.

It's also good with {{IconSAP|Leech}} as you can use a {{IconSAP|Lollipop}} on the Peacock, which swaps the attack and health of a pet - allowing the health to increase which lets you continue to buff its attack very quickly with Leech again. Alternatively, you can put Pita Bread on the Peacock to gain a lot of health without sacrificing attack.

Another good combo is with the {{IconSAP|Rat}}. Putting the Rat in front of the Peacock allows at least one easy buff to the unit, albeit with minor health lost and the fact that it’s dependent on your enemy’s board.

The '''Peacock''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Peacock takes damage, it gains attack. Leveling up the Peacock will increase the amount of attack it gains when hurt. 

==Strategy==
The '''Peacock''' is best paired with the {{IconSAP|Elephant}}, which will deal safe amounts of damage and it will be able to gain lots of attack in battle. Though, early on, it might be a good idea to give it {{IconSAP|Honey}}, as it will become a glass cannon.

Like most Pets with [[Hurt Pets|Hurt Abilities]], the Peacock benefits immensely from {{IconSAP|Garlic}} and later on, {{IconSAP|Lemon}} or {{IconSAP|Pita Bread}} due to their damage reductions or health gained when taking damage - something the Peacock wants to do while still being able to stay alive.

It's also good with {{IconSAP|Leech}} as you can use a {{IconSAP|Lollipop}} on the Peacock, which swaps the attack and health of a pet - allowing the health to increase which lets you continue to buff its attack very quickly with Leech again. Alternatively, you can put Pita Bread on the Peacock to gain a lot of health without sacrificing attack.

Another good combo is with the {{IconSAP|Rat}}. Putting the Rat in front of the Peacock allows at least one easy buff to the unit, albeit with minor health lost and the fact that it’s dependent on your enemy’s board.

==Trivia== 

*Peacocks are often depicted as very vain animals, taking great pride in their impressive plumage. Its ability in game could be interpreted as the Peacock becoming more and more enraged after being attacked.

The '''Flamingo''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Flamingo faints it buffs the stats of the two friends directly behind it. Leveling up the Flamingo will increase the strength of the buffs given. The Flamingo will never buff itself, nor will it buff any friend twice. If there are less than 2 friends behind it when it faints, its ability will be wasted.

The {{IconSAP|Mammoth}} is a direct upgrade to the Flamingo, targeting all friends with twice the buff amount upon faint. 
== Strategy==
The Flamingo is an effective Tier 2 unit, boasting above average attack as well as a useful ability both in battle and for scaling. This Pet is considered to some as a "You see it, you buy it" type of Pet, at least during early game.   

Similar to the {{IconSAP|Ant}}, but with stronger stats and a stronger ability. Giving the Flamingo a {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}} is similar to using a {{IconSAP|Salad Bowl}}, except it's available one tier earlier. You can also control which 2 pets get the 1/1 buff at the cost of an extra {{IconSAP|Gold}} (3 to buy the Flamingo and 1 to use the Sleeping Pill).  Flamingo is especially good with {{IconSAP|Ox}}, because pilling a flaming in front of an {{IconSAP|Ox}} is an extra attack, as well as the melon already on board.

It's very easy to fit a Flamingo on any team, and pill it later for a nice buff. Overall, the Flamingo is a nice pick in Tier 2 but is not recomended to be kept on a team for too long.

The '''Worm''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. At the start of turn the Worm will stock the food shop with a 2-gold {{IconSAP|Apple}}. Levelling up the Worm increases the stats given by the stocked Apple.

==Strategy==
Worm's ability to stock apples makes it great synergy with food-related scaling pets, such as {{IconSAP|Rabbit}} or {{IconSAP|Seal}}. Even without those two pets, Worm is a great scaling pet that can fit into most teams, providing convenient stat buffs, especially when levelled.

You can freeze Apples at the start of the turn to stockpile them for a big turn, such as waiting for a {{IconSAP|Bison}} on {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} or a Seal on {{IconSAP|Tier 5}}. You can freeze upwards of 4 Apples before the stocked food overtakes pet slots in the Shop.

In '''{{IconSAP|Custom Packs}}''', the Worm's Apple can be used to reliably trigger the {{IconSAP|Jerboa|name=Jerboa's}} ability, quickly scaling the whole team.

* The Worm stocking apples is likely a reference to the trope of worms inhabiting apples in school settings.

When the friend ahead of the Kangaroo attacks, the Kangaroo gains a buff to its stats. Leveling up the Kangaroo increases the buff it receives each time its ability is triggered. 

==Strategy==
The Kangaroo is best placed behind a beefy friend, such as an '''{{IconSAP|Ox|image=Ox.png}}''' (when it has its Melon ability active) or a {{IconSAP|Peacock|image=Peacock.png}} that can tank many hits to ensure that your Kangaroo will be a formidable pet that will go up next.

The '''Spider''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 2}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Spider faints, it summons a random tier 3 pet with set stats. Leveling up the Spider will increase the stats and level of the summoned pet.  

==Strategy==
Spider is a summoner that grants you access to pets from 1 tier higher than Spider itself. During battle, it has 60% chance of spawning a 2/2 with no combat abilities, 20% chance of spawning pets with good abilities ({{IconSAP|Camel}} and {{IconSAP|Sheep}}), and 20% chance of pets with potentially harmful abilities ({{IconSAP|Elephant}} and {{IconSAP|Badger}}). For early summon builds with {{IconSAP|Horse}}, giving {{IconSAP|Honey}} to Spider will spawn the {{IconSAP|Bee}} in front of the tier 3 pet, and if this was a {{IconSAP|Dog}} or {{IconSAP|Ox}}, the Bee would trigger their abilities and improve the battle capability of Spider as a whole. The abilities of Elephant and Badger can also be negated by putting a '''Hurt''' pet behind Spider, such as {{IconSAP|Peacock}}.

It's also commonly used with {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}} during shop tier 2 (turn 3 and 4) in order to gain tier 3 pets without requiring level up rewards. Alternatively, Spider can be leveled up first and then Pilled to immediately get a high leveled tier 3. The tradeoff is these pets will have below average stats, though the high level abilities are almost always worth it, and the lower stats can be bypassed by combining them with a copy from the shop.

[[File:Spider.wav]]

==Trivia==
The spider can be used for the lootbox challenge. The goal of which is to buy and faint 4 spiders by pilling a {{IconSAP|Hedgehog}} and winning with the pets it gives you. An alternative to this type of lootbox challenge is where you can get to sell or faint any of the pets you get out of the Spiders.

The '''Dodo''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of each battle, the Dodo gives the nearest friend in front of it a buff to its attack, equal to a percentage of the Dodo's attack. The percentage of the Dodo's own attack given is increased when the Dodo is leveled up.

==Strategy==
Dodo can be thought of as a 2-in-1 pet since any attack stats that go into Dodo also goes to the friend in front of it. It has good combos at almost all stages of the game and is a good target to dump stats onto and kept for later. A level 2 Dodo already gives away 100% of its attack stats, and often doesn't need to be leveled further.

Some Dodo combos include:
* {{IconSAP|Crab}}: A high stats Dodo will give both its attack and health to Crab and turn it into a stronger copy of Dodo.
* Dodo itself: Can be chained to pass more and more attack forward.
* {{IconSAP|Rhino}}: The extra attack can help it knock out enemies and trigger the ability.
* {{IconSAP|Rooster}}, {{IconSAP|Leopard}}: Their abilities get stronger with higher attacks, which Dodo can provide instantly without having to scale them.

==Game Sound==
[[File:Dodo.wav]]

==Trivia==
*The Dodo is tied with the {{IconSAP|Quetzalcoatlus}} as the lowest tier extinct pet, with the next lowest extinct pet being the {{IconSAP|Triceratops}} at Tier 5. 
*Dodo is likely the pet that has faced the most substantial nerfs, originally it would give 100% of its attack to the friend ahead and upon level up it would give 100% of its attack to the next two friends ahead.

The '''Dodo''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of each battle, the Dodo gives the nearest friend in front of it a buff to its attack, equal to a percentage of the Dodo's attack. The percentage of the Dodo's own attack given is increased when the Dodo is leveled up.

==Strategy==
Dodo can be thought of as a 2-in-1 pet since any attack stats that go into Dodo also goes to the friend in front of it. It has good combos at almost all stages of the game and is a good target to dump stats onto and kept for later. A level 2 Dodo already gives away 100% of its attack stats, and often doesn't need to be leveled further.

Some Dodo combos include:
* {{IconSAP|Crab}}: A high stats Dodo will give both its attack and health to Crab and turn it into a stronger copy of Dodo.
* Dodo itself: Can be chained to pass more and more attack forward.
* {{IconSAP|Rhino}}: The extra attack can help it knock out enemies and trigger the ability.
* {{IconSAP|Rooster}}, {{IconSAP|Leopard}}: Their abilities get stronger with higher attacks, which Dodo can provide instantly without having to scale them.

==Trivia==
*The Dodo is tied with the {{IconSAP|Quetzalcoatlus}} as the lowest tier extinct pet, with the next lowest extinct pet being the {{IconSAP|Triceratops}} at Tier 5. 
*Dodo is likely the pet that has faced the most substantial nerfs, originally it would give 100% of its attack to the friend ahead and upon level up it would give 100% of its attack to the next two friends ahead.

The '''Badger''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Badger faints, it will deal a percentage of its attack to the pet in front of and behind it, regardless of what team they are on. Levelling up the Badger increases the percentage of attack its ability will deal as damage.

== Strategy==
The Badger is a guy that damages the pet ahead and the pet behind, and realistically if it's gonna attack in battle and faint like a real MAN, it's gonna be an enemy and a friend. There are ways to mitigate this.

If the Badger is placed at the back, it will only hurt your opponent's pets. This means that the Badger can turn losses into draws, if its ability knocks out the last enemy pet. The Badger synergizes incredibly well with {{IconSAP|Honey}}, dubbed "Honey Badger". The {{IconSAP|Bee}} will win a draw if on the last pet, and the Badger can draw losses if in the last spot. This creates an infamous combo: the Badger faints the last enemy then creates a Bee, turning what would otherwise be a loss into a win. During the late game, {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} works better although the 1 damage probably won't amount too much. Still, it will against other Bees or Mushroom summoned Pets.

Badger shines in front, if you put a punk ass small guy behind it, minimizing the downside of the damage, most preferably a scaler like {{IconSAP|Giraffe}}, {{IconSAP|Cat}}, etc. The main benefit to this strategy is that it has a higher potential to destroy a big enemy unit because players will often put their strongest units near to the front, leading to this guy to trade with one opponent big guy or if scaled enough, two. Make sure to balance your scaling to the former so that it doesn't go overkill.

A strategy that is viable in a good amount of fields is to suck it up with hurt pets. A strategy is to use badgers to trigger hurt abilities of certain friends in combat. That's alright.

To counter the Badger, run {{IconSAP|Chili}}, {{IconSAP|Deer}} or {{IconSAP|Dolphin}}. This forces the Badger player to play differently and to {{IconSAP|Pear}} stuff above the 5 or 4 HP breakpoint. {{IconSAP|Chili}} is most preferable later on since taking one pet slot to counter badger rather than a perk slot feels kinda silly. In Versus you could also position stuff so that some guy of yours trades with it and all its damage goes to your small guy, minimizing damage from an opposing badger.

==Trivia==
*A Badger is one of the few Pets in the game that can one-shot a 50/50 Pet with melon armor. Others include 21+ attack Pets with peanut or a level 2 or higher Swordfish with 35+ attack.

The '''Dolphin''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''' . At the start of battle, the Dolphin will deal 4 damage to the enemy with the lowest health. Levelling up the Dolphin will increase the amount of times its ability triggers.

==Strategy==
Dolphin is designed to immediately disarm low health enemies and prevent them from triggering their abilities later into the battle. Its targets are often problematic pets that give stats or gain stats as the battle progresses such as {{IconSAP|Horse}}, {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}}, {{IconSAP|Dog}}, or just generally strong abilities with low health like {{IconSAP|Scorpion}} and {{IconSAP|Snake}} from later tiers. Its damage output is good enough for early game and almost guarantees that it will instantly knock something out at Start of battle.

At higher levels, it will be able to break through {{IconSAP|Melon}} to make sure its target is eliminated, or sniping multiple enemies at once. It has a superb synergy with {{IconSAP|Skunk}}: a level 3 Skunk with higher attack than Dolphin will put a strong enemy down to 1 health, then the Dolphin will target that enemy and likely knock it out.

The '''Giraffe''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''' . At the start of every turn, the Giraffe will buff the stats of the friend(s) ahead of it. Levelling up the Giraffe will increase the amount of friends it can target with its ability. 

==Strategy==
The Giraffe is respectable scaling for its tier. At Tier 3, you can look to place your giraffe behind a pet you will keep in the future battles, such as an {{IconSAP|Ox}} or a {{IconSAP|Badger}}.

When levelled up, you can buff animals more than one space ahead of it, allowing you to buff animals that require to be placed together without ruining their synergy, {{IconSAP|Camel}} and {{IconSAP|Elephant}}.

Starting from Tier 5 and higher, Giraffe's scaling is very easily outclassed by other scaling pets such as {{IconSAP|Penguin}} or {{IconSAP|Monkey}}. One should opt to a stronger scaling option as soon as possible.

==Trivia==
*The Giraffe is the only pet that says its name as part of its in game sound. In real life, giraffes are mute.
BUT WAIT!, scientist discovered that '''{{IconSAP|Giraffe|name=giraffe's}}''' giraffe's are NOT mute, they make some humming sounds, it makes it clear in the night.

** Unlike the Dromedary, which lives in the hot deserts of Arabia and North Africa, the Bactrian lives in cold steppes and mountains, and is therefore much fuzzier.
** The Camel’s sprite has long eyelashes because real camels do, to protect their eyes from the harsh sunlight of the desert.

'''Rabbit''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When a friendly pet eats any [[Food]], including Rabbit itself, Rabbit will give that pet additional health, up to three times per turn. Leveling up Rabbit increases the amount of health given.

==Strategy==
Rabbit gives extra health every time pets on the team receive foods and perks. At level 1, it's effectively multiplying the stats affect of all foods: 2x effect for {{IconSAP|Bread Crumbs}}, 1.5x for {{IconSAP|Apple}} and {{IconSAP|Salad Bowl}}, 1.25x for {{IconSAP|Pear}}, and so on. Multiple Rabbits can be used to give a more and more health.

Being a pure health scaler, it synergizes well with Hurt pets such as {{IconSAP|Peacock}} and {{IconSAP|Camel}} that love to be hit multiple times, but can also work for just building up a beefy tank that will stay until the end of the game. It also has synergies with {{IconSAP|Ox}}, {{IconSAP|Turtle}}, and {{IconSAP|Scorpion}} to give them extra health when they gain/give perks.

Just due to how efficient Rabbit is, it can easily snowball a pet into a 10/20 as early as turn 5, and can quickly be swapped out for something else once you've got yourself enough health scaling. In Turtle pack, a 20/40 will get to 50 health before you know it, but it will take a bit longer until it can reach 50 attack. You'll also be able to find an upgrade to Rabbit at tier 6: {{IconSAP|Cat}}.

The '''Ox''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When the nearest friend ahead of Ox faints, Ox will gain {{IconSAP|Melon}} [[Food Perks|Food perk]] and +1 attack. Leveling up Ox will increase the amount of times its ability can trigger per turn.

==Strategy==
Ox is one of the earliest pets in the game with access to a formidable ''tier 6'' perk. Melon is extremely powerful in all stages of the game. In early turns, since almost nothing can deal more than 20 damage, Ox is essentially invincible for one attack. It can also be thought of as having immunity against snipers breaking the Melon, since as long as it's not in front-most position, it will refresh its own Melon by the time it gets to attack.

It's a good target to focus stats on since the ability will remain useful until the end of the game. It synergies very well with all '''Faint''' pets such as {{IconSAP|Ant}}, {{IconSAP|Flamingo}}, {{IconSAP|Spider}}, and so on. {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill|name=Pilling}} any of these pets in front of Ox during shop phase will give it permanent Melon and a bonus +1 attack. Pilling a {{IconSAP|Turtle}} in front of Ox while it already has Melon will still give +1 attack while passing a new Melon over to another friend behind. Pill synergies also make it an amazing teammate with {{IconSAP|Shark}} later on.

At the same tier, Ox can combo with a front {{IconSAP|Badger}}. When Badger faints, it will pop the Melon, then Ox will immediately regain the Melon. Though this is rather risky if anything breaks the Melon beforehand and leaves Ox vulnerable to Badger's snipe.

The '''Dog''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. Whenever a friend is summoned, the Dog will gain a stat buff. However, the stats will only last until end of battle. Levelling up the Dog will increase the amount of stats gained for each friend summoned.  

==Strategy ==
The Dog has mediocre stats. It can be a heavy hitter for a few turns early on if you're buying and selling lots of pets, but tends to fall off quickly unless supported by a summoning team featuring units like the {{IconSAP|Sheep}} and the {{IconSAP|Fly}}. Even then, its ability is weak compared to that of pets like the {{IconSAP|Hippo}} and the {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}}. The dog pairs very well with the {{IconSAP|Dragon}} in the {{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}, but gets overshadowed by other buy/sell pets in customs like the {{IconSAP|Buffalo}}.

The '''Sheep''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Sheep faints, it summons two {{IconSAP|Ram|name=Rams}} with the same level as the Sheep. Levelling up the Sheep increases the stats of the summoned Rams. 

==Strategy ==
The Sheep synergizes with many Pets which make it a decent choice for early-game, but it does become less useful in the late game.

Being a summoning Pet, the Sheep works with the {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, allowing the Rams to dish out more damage.

Sheep also works with the {{IconSAP|Ox}} and {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}}, as it allows Ox and Kangaroo to trigger their effect '''twice''' if placed behind a Sheep.

When it comes to [[Food]], it is advisable to give it {{IconSAP|Meat Bone}} early on and replace it with {{IconSAP|Steak}} if still used late game. You can use a {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}} on a Level 2 Sheep can result in a '''Level 3 Ram''', if the two Level 2 Rams are merged. This allows Sheep to even work with {{IconSAP|Bison}}, as long as the Player doesn't mess up by '''not having enough space''' for the 2 Rams to spawn.

Though, it falls off as soon as stronger summoning pets, such as {{IconSAP|Deer}} and {{IconSAP|Fly}}, and even giving free stats or advantage to the enemies with {{IconSAP|Hippo}} or {{IconSAP|Rhino}} on their team.

Overall, the Sheep is a great early game Pet and is very versatile, and its effect is incredibly useful even without the use of other Pets, however does get outshined by other pets in late-game.

The '''Skunk''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of battle, the Skunk will reduce the health of the highest health enemy by a percentage of its total health, rounded up. Leveling up the Skunk will increase the percentage number that the enemy's health is reduced by.

==Strategy==
Skunk is an anti-scaling pet that deals percentage-based damage instead of a flat amount of damage, and thus become stronger the more stats the enemy has. The health reduction can be devastating and forces the enemy to build a well rounded team with multiple high stat pets instead of putting all their eggs in one basket. At level 3, Skunk will instantly cripple an enemy down to 1 health for an easy knock out.

It should be noted that Skunk's ability is incapable of directly knocking out an enemy and will always need follow up damage to defeat them. This can be problematic against defensive food perks like {{IconSAP|Melon}} that may allow the Skunked enemy to still get one or multiple attacks off. Pairing Skunk with snipers like {{IconSAP|Dolphin}} can mitigate this issue and eliminate the problematic enemy immediately.

If you're running a scaling focused team, there are next to no counters against Skunk beside just scaling more pets. Though as powerful as it is, Skunk is extremely ineffective against summon teams and pets that gain stats as the battle progresses such as {{IconSAP|Shark}}.

The '''Hippo''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Whenever Hippo knocks out an enemy, it gains a hefty amount of attack and health, up to 3 times per battle. Leveling up the Hippo will increase the amount of stats it gains upon a successful knock out.

==Strategy==
Hippo is a counter pet designed to steamroll through summon builds. It will "heal" itself after each knock out, and is best paired with defensive food perks such as {{IconSAP|Garlic}} and {{IconSAP|Melon}} to maximize its chance at surviving and knocking out more pets. {{IconSAP|Chili}} is another good option since it can knock out the second enemy and trigger Hippo's ability. Pairing Hippo with a front {{IconSAP|Rat}} can give it a few additional buffs from knocking out the {{IconSAP|Dirty Rat|name=Dirty Rat(s)}}.

Scaling a front-most Hippo is a common strategy to win rounds in mid game, as it can be quite unstoppable against summoners around the same turns. A backline Hippo can also work to clean up the weak enemies. Even against scaled units, if your Hippo is stronger, it can knock out the enemy's scaled unit and activate its Knock Out ability, steamrolling the usually weaker backline.

The hippo may be an excellent early to mid game option, even being good near the start of Tier 6, but keep in mind that as the game gets further, you will likely face highly scaled units that make it hard for the Hippo's ability to shine, as well as Summon Comps having strong pets such as '''{{IconSAP|Turkey}}''' combined with a '''{{IconSAP|Tiger}}''' or a '''{{IconSAP|Parrot}}''' that can overwhelm your Hippo.

The '''Bison''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the end of turn, the Bison gains a boost to its stats, but only if there is at least one other level 3 pet on the team. Leveling up the Bison will increase the amount of stats it gains.

A level 3 Bison will '''not''' scale itself.

== Strategy==
Bison is a mid game self scaler that can carry the team all the way until the game ends. It requires a level 3 friend on the team, which can be achieved early on by hunting for duplicates and leveling up tier 1 and 2 pets. {{IconSAP|Fish}} and {{IconSAP|Otter}} are solid targets to push for level 3, but anything else will also work. By late game, you can either get rid of this level 3 in favor of stronger pets or other forms of scaling, or level up a different pet to level 3 to maintain Bison's scaling.

One common strategy is keeping half leveled pets until turn 5, then leveling all of them up for a chance to spawn an early Bison. This becomes even more effective if the level ups result in a level 3 pet, which means you can have a self scaling Bison immediately on that turn.

Having 2 level 3 Bisons on the team that buff each other is a strong strategy, but hard to come by.

Beware of these common pitfalls while running Bison: 
*'''Buying Bison before you have a level 3''': This is not inherently bad, but you should be able to reevaluate when it's time to ditch the Bison if the level 3 is taking too long to show up. Bison scaling takes up 2 slots, not 1, ditching both these slots might just be what's necessary to turn the run around.
*'''Keeping a deadweight level 3 for too long''': Since this level 3 is often a low tier pet, you should not overvalue Bison's buff over a potentially stronger pet.
*'''Forgetting Bison needs a level 3 friend''':  Newer players can make the mistake of selling their level 3 pet in favor for another pet, forgetting that it is needed for Bison to scale.

Abilities that deal direct damage can be stronger than what it might look at first glance as you are dealing damage without taking damage back.

|level_2='''Faint''': Give {{IconSAP|Melon}} [[Food Perks|perk]] to the two nearest friends behind.
|level_3='''Faint''': Give {{IconSAP|Melon}} [[Food Perks|perk]] to the three nearest friends behind.
}}
The '''Turtle''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When Turtle faints, it gives the nearest friend behind it {{IconSAP|Melon}} [[Food Perks|perk]], overriding other [[Food Perks|Food Perk]] or [[Ailments|Ailment]] they had previously. When leveled up, Turtle will give Melon perk to more friends behind.

==Strategy==
Turtle is most commonly bought and {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill|name=Pilled}} to gain early access to Melon. When kept on the team, it combos best with scaling teams that benefit more from the protection of Melon than the attack stats from {{IconSAP|Steak}} or synergies with {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}. It's commonly put directly ahead of the pet with the highest attack/health in the team, which usually means it'll be the front-most pet while the strongest pet is in the second position. This accomplishes 3 things:

#'''Refreshing the team's Melon''': Snipers like {{IconSAP|Mosquito}}, {{IconSAP|Blowfish}}, {{IconSAP|Leopard}} or Ailment pets from other packs like {{IconSAP|Bat}} or {{IconSAP|Toad}} can strip the team off Melons. Turtle can counter this by giving Melon afterward.
#'''Breaking the enemy's Melon''': A common strategy is having a strong pet in front with a defensive food perk. If that perk was Melon, Turtle will pop it and allows our strong pet now with Melon to face against one without Melon.
#'''Countering {{IconSAP|Scorpion}}''': Similarly, Scorpion is usually in front and will be knocked out by our Turtle.

Turtle also "synergizes" with Melon itself: It will skip over friends that already have Melons, so putting more Melons on your team simply ensure they will always have protections both at Start of battle and during battle.

===Custom packs===
By combining all of this with a pet like the {{IconSAP|Elephant Seal}} or the {{IconSAP|Axolotl}}, you can gain massive amounts of stats whenever your turtle faints. Another strategy would be to combine the Turtle with {{IconSAP|Microbe}} or {{IconSAP|Pandoras Box}} from {{IconSAP|Bad Dog}}. Pandoras Box will give your whole team perks/ailments, but none of them will matter because the Turtle will replace all of those bad perks/ailments with {{IconSAP|Melon}}.

==Trivia== 
*The Turtle is the mascot of Super Auto Pets (and this wiki).
**It appears on the game's desktop and mobile icons.
***The turtle sprite is actually a green tortoise.
****There has appeared to be a humanoid version of the turtle called “Turtle Tyranny” when the turtle is overpowered, (clip appears in the official youtube channel).

Another strategy would be to combine the Turtle with {{IconSAP|Microbe}} or {{IconSAP|Pandoras Box}} from {{IconSAP|Bad Dog}}. Pandoras Box will give your whole team perks/ailments, but none of them will matter because the Turtle will replace all of those bad perks/ailments with {{IconSAP|Melon}}.

**It appears on the game's desktop and mobile icons.
***The turtle sprite is actually a green tortoise.

The '''Squirrel''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of each turn, Squirrel will reduce the {{IconSAP|gold}} cost of all [[Foods]] that are currently in the shop. Leveling up the Squirrel will further reduce the costs of the foods.

==Strategy==
Squirrel relies on investing in freezing certain foods to purchase them at a discounted price on future turns. Most Foods at {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} and above are worth freezing, with current team synergy having a heavy hand in what should be prioritised. {{IconSAP|Chocolate}} will almost always be valuable to any team and is often worth making use of the Squirrel's ability to purchase more easily.

Squirrel has good synergy with most [[Food Pets]], specifically the Pets that are able to increase the amount of stats gained from purchasing foods like {{IconSAP|Rabbit}}, {{IconSAP|Seal}} and {{IconSAP|Rabbit}}. These pets further increase the value of reducing the cost of shop Foods due to the extra stats they are able to give per gold spent.

The Squirrel also synergises somewhat effectively with {{IconSAP|Worm}}. If the Squirrel has less attack than the Worm then the Worm will stock its 2-gold {{IconSAP|Apple}} and then the Squirrel will discount it in addition to the other shop foods. This is especially effective with early Rabbit(s) and in '''{{IconSAP|Custom Packs}}''' with {{IconSAP|Jerboa}} teams.

At level 1, it affects the {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}}, At level 2, it affects the Worm's {{IconSAP|Apple}}, At level 3, it is easy since all food are now 0 gold. However, When you roll the shop, the cost of all food will become normal.

==Trivia==
Both sprites of the Squirrel is holding an Acorn.

The Squirrel pet is one of three pets based on a squirrel, the others being the {{IconSAP|Albino Squirrel}} and the {{IconSAP|Giant Squirrel}}.

The '''Deer''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Deer faints, it summons a {{IconSAP|Bus}} with {{IconSAP|Chili}}. Levelling up the Deer increases the level and stats of the summoned Bus.

==Strategy==
Since Bus has relatively high stats and comes with a strong tier 5 perk, Deer can be thought of as effectively having 12/5 base stats (2/2 + 5/3 + 5/0). It wants to be knocked out ASAP to get to Bus. Deer and Bus can sweep plenty of low stats pets and can be oppressive if it's found early. It combines well with all summon supporters such as {{IconSAP|Whale}}, {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, {{IconSAP|Tiger}}, {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}, and so on.

==Trivia==
Deer is one of the few mascots that reference real life, where a hurried driver (probably represented by a chili bus) can end up running over the clueless deer, which will end up fainting (just like in the game).

The '''Whale''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. At the Start of battle, Whale will swallow (knock out) the nearest friend ahead. Then when Whale faints, it will summon that friend at level 1, with identical stats as before it was swallowed, but without any perks. Leveling up the Whale will increase the level of the summoned friend.

Summoned friends are considered "new" pets, with no memory of their old selves before being swallowed. For example if a {{IconSAP|Parrot}} was swallowed, it will not keep the copied abilities when summoned.

Whale is ''not'' considered a '''Faint''' pet, and does not synergize with pets that call for Faint abilities.

==Strategy==
Whale synergies well with all Faint pets, and effectively triggering their abilities twice. Pairing it with a {{IconSAP|Deer}} to summon the {{IconSAP|Bus}} immediately, then later the Whale will also summon another Deer for another Bus. Pairing it with {{IconSAP|Turtle}} to gain multiple {{IconSAP|Melon|name=Melons}}, {{IconSAP|Flamingo}} and later {{IconSAP|Mammoth}} to get multiple stats buffs. It can also synergize with {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}, for example a unique combo is {{IconSAP|Whale}} + {{IconSAP|Scorpion}} + {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} for 2 instakills.

It can also be used to "protect" friends from damage such as Start of battle snipers: The friend is safe inside Whale until it's released, although this comes at a cost of their perks.

A special interaction is with {{IconSAP|Tiger}}. Putting Tiger behind the Whale will cause it to swallow up to 2 friends ahead, then summon all of them on faint. Tiger will also double the ability of whatever Whale releases.

The '''Parrot''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the end of turn, Parrot copies the ability from the nearest friend ahead and reverts back to its original ability when the battle ends. The level of the ability copied is the same as the Parrot's level, regardless of the level of the friend it copied from.

Due to being an '''End turn''' ability, copying another End turn pet will not trigger Parrot again. For example, copying a {{IconSAP|Bison}} won't make the Parrot buff itself.

==Strategy==
Parrot can be used as a duplicate of any pet in the team during battle, which makes it a unique pivot pet. It can be bought preemptively then later put a higher tier pet in front of the Parrot for their level 2 or 3 abilities. Parrots can also form a chain by putting them in highest to lowest attack, front to back order, then each Parrot will pass its copied ability to the one behind.

It's often used to copy strong in-battle abilities like {{IconSAP|Crocodile}}, {{IconSAP|Leopard}} or summoning pets like {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, {{IconSAP|Shark}}, etc. Keeping a high leveled/high stats Parrot will give you an immense power spike once you pivot into these pets.

==Trivia==
* The Parrot seems to be based off of the red-crowned amazon.

The '''Scorpion''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When summoned, it will gain {{IconSAP|Peanut}} perk, which instantly knocks out any enemy that's hurt by Scorpion. Scorpion's ability does not change on level up.

==Strategy==
Scorpion is an extremely cheap investment that can instantly take out big enemies with high stats. It's generally put frontmost since this is where high scaled enemies are often positioned. Due to being designed as an anti-scaler, it does not work well against summon teams.

Despite having low stats, it poses a very serious threat and is something most teams have to prepare counterplays for. This often means putting {{IconSAP|Melon}} on the frontmost pet to block the Scorpion, putting a weak pet in front as a meatshield, or bringing along a {{IconSAP|Dolphin}} to snipe it.

However, there are also counters to these counterplays. When paired with {{IconSAP|Whale}} and/or {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}, it can break the Melon/knock out the meatshield/tank the snipe, then revive with Peanut to knock out the big enemy. A Scorpion with 21 attack or higher can also hurt the enemy through Melon and knock them out in a single hit.

Scorpion also has some terrifying synergy with {{IconSAP|Rabbit}} as a buff target, since Scorpion doesn't care about the lack of attack scaling provided by Rabbit! To the same extent, multiple {{IconSAP|Armadillo}} + Scorpion can save you from scaling boards even with your back against the wall. Be careful of start of battle snipes though, your scorpion is very vulnerable before the Armadillo activates!

Overall it's a very simple yet dangerous pet that can fit on almost any team. It can help scaling teams to gain advantage over other scalers, or help summon teams to get rid of the troublesome tanks in the front.

==Trivia==

Scorpion's peanuts are deadly, a play on the common allergy to peanuts!

The '''Crocodile''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of each battle, the Crocodile deals 8 {{IconSAP|damage|nolink=yes}} to the Pet at the back of the enemy team. Levelling up the Crocodile will increase the amount of times it deals 8 damage to the backmost enemy pet.

==Strategy==
Crocodile is a simple-yet-effective anti-backline pet. Enemies in backmost positions tend to have low stats and abilities that will become troublesome during battle such as {{IconSAP|Shark}}, {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, and {{IconSAP|Fly}}. In any cases, Crocodile will deal a substantial amount of damage to them, then repeat the snipe at higher levels to either break through their defensive perks to ensure a knockout, or if they have already been knocked out, damage the next enemies in the back.

While Crocodile ability stands on its own with no obvious combos, it can be very effective when paired with other '''Start of battle''' snipers and repeaters such as {{IconSAP|Dolphin}}, {{IconSAP|Parrot}}, other Crocodiles, and {{IconSAP|Tiger}}. Crocodile is exceptionally powerful against most summon teams, and more snipes means knocking out more pets to really crush these builds.

The '''Rhino''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Rhino Knocks out an opponent, the Rhino will deal damage to the first enemy (dealing double damage to Tier 1 Pets). If an enemy is knocked out by the Rhino's ability, the Rhino's ability will trigger again. Levelling up the Rhino will increase the amount of damage its ability deals.

==Strategy==
When you see a Lvl 3 Rhino You, know your cooked, Rhino's good. Like. good good. Yknow. It's big as hell, works with {{IconSAP|Monkey}} or {{IconSAP|Tiger}} super well, and yeah it triggers again if it knocks out an enemy via ability. It's good against summoning teams (more often levelled if you need to since the 4 hp threshold from summons can be mitigated with various summons. note that it does double damage to tier 1s and, like, all tokens are Tier 1s man), and it's good against scaling teams since it can pop {{IconSAP|Melon}}s. Against it you should position stuff so it doesn't pop melons, preferably using stuff that's above 4, 8, and (rarely) 12 health.

A rhino with chilli can really work with a level 2 {{IconSAP|Rat}} for the rhino to attack twice if the enemy has 2 empty slots on their team.

Also it procs hurt triggers like {{IconSAP|Blowfish}} or {{IconSAP|Gorilla}}. Maybe you can use that someday against it. Watch out for your own {{IconSAP|Summon Pets|name=summons|image=Cricket_Icon.png}} for the latter.

The '''Monkey''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. At the end of turn, the Monkey will provide a big stat buff to the front-most friendly pet. Leveling up the Monkey will increase the amount of stats it gives. 

==Strategy==
In Turtle pack, Monkey is the highest tier passive scaler, requiring no additional actions while giving a consistent amount of stats each turn. It's much easier to use compared to active scalers like {{IconSAP|Cat}} and {{IconSAP|Dragon}}, which require you to properly balance gold. While it only targets the front-most pet, this is often where you would put your strongest pet, and multiple Monkeys will buff the same pet, so they can easily snowball an already high stats pet or one with powerful ability into a 50/50.

Monkey's biggest weakness is its rigidity. If you want a pet to be buffed by Monkey, that pet ''has'' to stay in front. This makes their positioning predictable and they can be targeted by common counters like {{IconSAP|Scorpion}}. It also limits your team's composition: it can't be used to buff pets that are designed to stay behind like {{IconSAP|Dodo}} or {{IconSAP|Parrot}}, running your own Scorpion with a Monkey on the team often means wasting the Monkey's buff, you can't use Monkey to buff a high level {{IconSAP|Rooster}} since it'd waste the {{IconSAP|Chick|name=Chicks}}, and so on. And after you're satisfied with a pet's stats and want to buff another one, you'll have to push that big pet behind and weaken the team's structure.

In Golden pack, Monkey can be obtained by putting {{IconSAP|Banana}} perk on a {{IconSAP|Manatee}} and allowing it to faint. You can read more about this on [[Manatee|Manatee's page]].

The '''Armadillo''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} pet, available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of battle, the Armadillo will give a health buff to its friends ''and'' enemies, including itself. Leveling up the Armadillo increases the amount of health it gives.

==Strategy==
The Armadillo can be used to beefen up a summoning comp, including of pets such as '''{{IconSAP|Turkey}}''' or '''{{IconSAP|Fly}}''', to ensure that they do not die easily to snipers available on Tier 5 onwards, notably Crocodile or Leopard. 

Hurt abilities like '''{{IconSAP|Camel}}''' and '''{{IconSAP|Gorilla}}''' can benefit more off gaining health than other pets.

Attack Buffing pets like '''{{IconSAP|Dodo}}''' , '''{{IconSAP|Seal}}'''  and '''{{IconSAP|Fire Ant}}''' can help balance out stats. However, if a high health pet has '''{{IconSAP|Peanuts}}''' like '''{{IconSAP|Scorpion}}''' or through '''{{IconSAP|Walrus}}''', they can destroy multiple enemies without any additional attack required.

One should be wary of the downside of using Armadillo, as it also buffs the health of the enemy pets. It can be very powerful, but only under circumstances where you know your team will benefit more off of its ability than the enemy.

You can also combo Armadillo with '''{{IconSAP|Skunk}}''' to lower the enemy's HP after Armadillo's health ability goes off. Be sure to increase Armadillo's attack stat and make sure it is higher than the Skunk, so that the Armadillo's ability goes first.

The '''Armadillo''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} pet, available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of battle, the Armadillo will give a health buff to its friends ''and'' enemies, including itself. Leveling up the Armadillo increases the amount of health it gives.

==Strategy==
The Armadillo can be used to beefen up a summoning comp, including of pets such as '''{{IconSAP|Turkey}}''' or '''{{IconSAP|Fly}}''', to ensure that they do not die easily to snipers available on Tier 5 onwards, notably Crocodile or Leopard. 

Hurt abilities like '''{{IconSAP|Camel}}''' and '''{{IconSAP|Gorilla}}''' can benefit more off gaining health than other pets.

Attack Buffing pets like '''{{IconSAP|Dodo}}''' , '''{{IconSAP|Seal}}'''  and '''{{IconSAP|Fire Ant}}''' can help balance out stats. However, if a high health pet has '''{{IconSAP|Peanuts}}''' like '''{{IconSAP|Scorpion}}''' or through '''{{IconSAP|Walrus}}''', they can destroy multiple enemies without any additional attack required.

One should be wary of the downside of using Armadillo, as it also buffs the health of the enemy pets. It can be very powerful, but only under circumstances where you know your team will benefit more off of its ability than the enemy.

You can also combo Armadillo with '''{{IconSAP|Skunk}}''' to lower the enemy's HP after Armadillo's health ability goes off. Be sure to increase Armadillo's attack stat and make sure it is higher than the Skunk, so that the Armadillo's ability goes first.

The '''Cow''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When Cow is bought, it removes all foods from the shop and adds 2 free {{IconSAP|Milk}} that each gives +1 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}} and +2 {{IconSAP|health|nolink=yes}}. Leveling up the Cow will spawn {{IconSAP|Better Milk}} and then {{IconSAP|Best Milk}}, with increasingly improved stat buffs.

Cow has an additional hidden ability: When given {{IconSAP|Chocolate}}, it will spawn 2 free {{IconSAP|Chocolate Milk}} that only gives +1 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}} and no health. This ability also improves upon leveling up and spawns Better Chocolate Milk and Best Chocolate Milk.

==Strategy==
Cow is a versatile scaler with unparalleled efficiency. It brings consistency to the food hunt as each Cow is equal to 2 ''targeted'' foods with stat effects, able to trigger food abilities twice while giving a good amount of stats.

The most common strategy is buy-selling Cows, since it's 2 gold while giving the same amount of stats as {{IconSAP|Sushi}}. Another strategy is keeping a Cow on the team then stacking copies on top, which will continuously give more stats with stronger Milks. Even keeping Cow on the team for one turn can be worthwhile, since it gives more stats on that turn than any other scaler from tier 5 and below while having much higher base stats. Furthermore unlike other '''Buy''' pets, giving Chocolates to Cow isn't a complete waste as it can still give stats through Chocolate Milk, so this can be useful in accelerating Cow's level ups.

Note that Milk will spawn after Level up rewards and replace any pets that might be in the 2 right-most spaces in the food shop. Chocolate Milk on the other hand will spawn ''before'' Level up rewards and can be overridden by pets being pushed to the right.

==Trivia==
* Chocolate Milk used to give +2/+1 in the September 29th 2022 test build.

The '''Seal''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Seal eats [[Food]], it buffs the stats of two random friends. Levelling up the Seal will increase the amount of stats the two random friends will receive. 

==Strategy==
Seal is a Pet that fits in into [[Food Pets|Food teams]] perfectly.

Seal synergizes with {{IconSAP|Cat}} as it'll gain a multiplicative buff from Food while buffing other animals, allowing it to get stronger faster. 

Seal also synergizes with {{IconSAP|Rabbit}}, at it will gain extra health from the Food. 

Some other Pets that can be effectively run with a Seal are the {{IconSAP|Squirrel}} and the {{IconSAP|Sauropod}}. These pets decrease the effective cost of shop food and can even create a net gain of {{IconSAP|Gold}} if both are run on the same team and with enough experience.  

===Tips and Tricks===
* You could feed your Seal the same [[Food Perks|Food perk]] so it buffs your pets while still keeping the perk you would like (i.e. feeding your Seal with {{IconSAP|Garlic}} perk more Garlic.)
*It is recommended feeding {{IconSAP|Chocolate}} to your Seal when it is '''1 experience away''' from leveling up. This is because the buff your Seal would give is based on the level it would be at post Chocolate.
*Though risky, it might sometimes be better to buy Food that has random targeting (e.g. {{IconSAP|Pizza}}), as it has a chance to buff '''the Seal and other Pets'''.

The '''Rooster''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Rooster faints, it summons a {{IconSAP|Chick}} with the same level as the Rooster, 1 {{IconSAP|health|nolink=yes}} and half the {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}} that the Rooster had when it fainted. Levelling up the Rooster increases the amount of Chicks summoned.

==Strategy==
The Roosters power comes from value that giving it attack will yield. Giving the Rooster any number of attack is 50% more effective even at level 1, increasing in 50% intervals as you level it up. This makes the Rooster an excellent candidate for scaling and a perfect duo with the {{IconSAP|Dodo}}.

The maximum amount of attack for the summoned chick(s) is 25 attack but can be paired by a {{IconSAP|German Shepherd}} to reach 50 attack.

==Trivia==
'''{{IconSAP|Rooster}}''' are the few animals that their gender is known, as a Rooster is always a male.

if it were a female, it would become a chicken, hence theirs already one '''{{IconSAP|Chicken}}'''.

The '''Shark''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Each time one of its friends faints, the Shark gains a moderate amount of stats. Leveling up the Shark will increase the amount of stats it gains.  

==Strategy==
Shark is a pet that gets stronger as the battle progresses, similar to {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}} or {{IconSAP|Camel}} combos from earlier tiers. A back-most Shark will have at minimum 4 faint triggers and gain +8/+8, so it can already be a 10/10 on the turn it's bought. Shark fits nicely in summon teams that can feed it with even more faint triggers. It also gets some extra benefits from {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill|name=Pilling}} pets during shop phases, and will be very happy to see {{IconSAP|Turtle}} Pill and {{IconSAP|Mammoth}} Pill. 

Shark is a good counter to {{IconSAP|Skunk}}, it can either tank the health reduction then gain them back during battle, or dodge the Skunk completely due to starting out at lower health. However since it's usually placed behind and has low base stats, it's very susceptible to {{IconSAP|Crocodile}} as well as other snipers.

The '''Turkey''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When a friend is summoned, the Turkey gives it a buff to its stats. Leveling up the Turkey increases the amount of stats it gives to the summoned friends.

==Strategy==
Turkey is one of the cornerstones of summon builds, it is often a must-have and a target that all summon builds want to hard roll for. It's flexible, powerful, and easy to use.

The most obvious usage is giving stats to all summoned pets, allowing them to not only deal more damage, but also potentially survive more attacks. Having multiple Turkeys, or pairing it with {{IconSAP|Parrot}} or {{IconSAP|Tiger}} and you can flood the team with stats, creating unstoppable {{IconSAP|Bus|name=Buses}}, {{IconSAP|Chick|name=Chicks}}, {{IconSAP|Zombie Fly|name=Zombie Flies}}, and so on.

Another use is for pivoting: each pet bought into an empty slot will receive a great amount of stats. Every new Turkey will be buffed by the ones already on the team, and they will continuously get bigger and stronger. If you find an early Turkey, it's often possible to dump whatever you have been running and pivot completely to a summon build. {{IconSAP|Canned Food}} will also help in making these pivots easier.

Due to being crucial to summon builds, should the Turkey be sniped, the entire team can collapse. It's also often placed at the back where it'll be vulnerable to {{IconSAP|Crocodile}}. So even though it doesn't really need it, it's recommended to still give the Turkey some stats and defensive perks such as {{IconSAP|Melon}} or {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}.

The '''Turkey''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When a friend is summoned, the Turkey gives it a buff to its stats. Leveling up the Turkey increases the amount of stats it gives to the summoned friends.

==Strategy==
Turkey is one of the cornerstones of summon builds, it is often a must-have and a target that all summon builds want to hard roll for. It's flexible, powerful, and easy to use.

The most obvious usage is giving stats to all summoned pets, allowing them to not only deal more damage, but also potentially survive more attacks. Having multiple Turkeys, or pairing it with {{IconSAP|Parrot}} or {{IconSAP|Tiger}} and you can flood the team with stats, creating unstoppable {{IconSAP|Bus|name=Buses}}, {{IconSAP|Chick|name=Chicks}}, {{IconSAP|Zombie Fly|name=Zombie Flies}}, and so on.

Another use is for pivoting: each pet bought into an empty slot will receive a great amount of stats. Every new Turkey will be buffed by the ones already on the team, and they will continuously get bigger and stronger. If you find an early Turkey, it's often possible to dump whatever you have been running and pivot completely to a summon build. {{IconSAP|Canned Food}} will also help in making these pivots easier.

Due to being crucial to summon builds, should the Turkey be sniped, the entire team can collapse. It's also often placed at the back where it'll be vulnerable to {{IconSAP|Crocodile}}. So even though it doesn't really need it, it's recommended to still give the Turkey some stats and defensive perks such as {{IconSAP|Melon}} or {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}.

The '''Leopard''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. At the start of battle, the Leopard will deal {{IconSAP|damage|nolink=yes}} to a random enemy, equal to 50% of the Leopard's current {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}}. Leveling up the Leopard will increase the amount of random enemies it will hit with its ability.

==Strategy==
Leopard has an integral role in Turtle Pack as its strongest late game buff target. In games where you're able to make it to tier 6 with a lot of lives, buffing and supporting a Leopard is often one of the safest ways to close a game out, as its snipes are both neutrally devastating and can deal with utility effects such as summon teams, {{IconSAP|Melon}} or {{IconSAP|Scorpion}}. 

However, you can often be quite vulnerable in the first couple turns of taking a Leopard - its low hp is quite vulnerable and its ability weak for the turn you buy it on. Leopard is often a commitment to use your remaining lives to set up a board with an incredibly high ceiling that will safely win once you've scaled stats and levels enough.


Leopard's best friend by far is {{IconSAP|Monkey}}, as its targeted or 'tall' scaling is unmatched. {{IconSAP|Cat}} and {{IconSAP|Dragon}} are both great options too if you can, but since Monkey is available earlier in the game you can often already be set up with multiple copies of monkey and switch from whatever you were buffing before to buffing your Leopard. The value of this linear scaling on Leopard can also be multiplied by {{IconSAP|Tiger}}, as well as finding levels on Leopard, and increasing how many of these high damage snipes you get is just as necessary as stacking buffs onto it - this is another reason why the free passive scaling of monkey can be more useful than cat or dragon, freeing your gold up to be spent on chocolate and tiger. 


Leopard's importance is also as a payoff to certain early-midgame strategies that are played with its existence in mind:

- {{IconSAP|Dodo}} is the best example of this, as a rare but solid buff target in the early game its ability to convert games past turn 9 are almost entirely dependent on its synergy with Leopard. It's important to keep your dodo high on attack, so it will always buff the Leopard's attack before it shoots its snipe and massively buff its damage output. 

- Leopard is also one of the best payoffs for buffing a {{IconSAP|Parrot}} during the midgame, allowing you to almost skip that aforementioned stage of vulnerability by already having a high stat, high level pet to take on its ability. 

===End game===
A level 3 Leopard with 50 attack will deal a total of 75 snipe damage, this makes Leopard one of the simplest yet most effective pets in end game teams. In scenarios with teams full of max stats pets, having multiple Leopards/Tigers can break through any defensive perks and eliminate everything in sight.

Since these teams can knock out through defensive perks, it can be better to go for powerful summoners such as {{IconSAP|Beluga Whale}} to fight the post-snipe battle instead of trying to survive the carpet bomb. Alternatively, {{IconSAP|Humphead Wrasse}} can work as a hard counter against Leopard.

These 0 damage shots do not trigger [[Hurt (Trigger)|Hurt]] abilities, do not interact with defensive food perks and aren't affected by ailments. However, they ''are'' affected by {{IconSAP|Pineapple}}, which will increase the damage to 2.
