The '''Boar''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. Before every attack, the Boar will gain a buff to its stats. Leveling up the Boar will increase the size of the buff.  

The stats the Boar gains through its ability are not permanent, and are not retained outside of battle.

==Strategy==
While the Boar may appear to be a better {{IconSAP|Hippo}}, it being a Tier 6 means that scaling it to effective stats is harder, as it appears later in the game. At higher levels it can still serve as an effective summon pet counter but due to the general uncertainty of the teams one will face, it isn't a very reliable investment.  

During later turns where 50/50 pets are frequent, the Boar's ability will usually not be enough to avoid being knocked-out in 1 or 2 hits. But due to the Boar's high base stats it is extremely effective when summoned from an {{IconSAP|Eagle}}, especially if leveled due to the way base stats worked when summoned at a higher level. A Boar summoned from a level 3 Eagle will have 30 attack and 18 health and will gain +12/+6 before each attack making it an effective 42/24 and a very lucky summon from the Eagle.   

Following similar logic, giving a level 3 Boar a {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} will enable it to be summoned again as a level 3 1/1 that will buff itself to be a 13/7 and potentially higher if not taken out in one hit. This can be combined with a {{IconSAP|Seagull}} that also has Mushroom to continuously summon 13/7s. This may seem effective but keep in mind that if one has the capability to get a level 3 Tier 6, {{IconSAP|Octopus}} is a much more effective choice and works in a larger range of scenarios.

Like the Hippo, it can function quite effectively with a {{IconSAP|Tiger}}, helping it gain more health and making it more likely to survive an enemy attack. This is further amplified with a {{IconSAP|Lemon}} or {{IconSAP|Garlic}}, allowing for it to better survive - especially against an already ideal enemy team of [[Summon Pets]].

==Trivia==
*The Boar was the first ever pet to be added into a pack ''after'' the pack's initial release and also the first pet to ever be added on it's own in an update.

The '''Tiger''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. While in battle, whenever the nearest pet ahead of the Tiger triggers their ability, they will immediately trigger it again but this time at the same level as the Tiger.

That bad boy works with '''bold texts''', say, '''Hurt''', '''Faint''', '''Friend summoned''', yeah you know the deal. It doesn't work with '''End Turn''' or '''Start of turn''' abilities like {{IconSAP|Giraffe}},{{IconSAP|Monkey}}, or, well, another Tiger.

Friends repeating their abilities won't deplete additional triggers. For example: Each time a friend faints, {{IconSAP|Fly}} would summon 2 {{IconSAP|Zombie Fly|name=Zombie Flies}} but only lose 1 trigger.

==Strategy==
Tiger is a unique supporter that upgrades combat abilities, often making that pet twice as strong. For example, putting a Tiger behind {{IconSAP|Snake}} will make the Snake shoots twice each time it's triggered.

At the moment (08/01/2026), {{IconSAP|Tiger}} has been changed for to deplete triggers, so, you will get faster activations, but they won't last too much!


'''{{IconSAP|Tiger}}''' + '''{{IconSAP|Rhino}}''' is a great combo!, it can wipe out pets with a single attack!. '''

{{ARTICLEPAGENAME}}

Tiger's ability is a bit similar to {{IconSAP|Parrot}}. But while they both share a similar audience, they each have their own strengths, use cases, and pets that they work better on. For example, while both {{IconSAP|Tiger}} {{IconSAP|Turkey}} and {{IconSAP|Parrot}} {{IconSAP|Turkey}} serve the same purpose for summon teams, Parrot can be found much earlier and would be higher level than Tiger. An example would be '''Hurt''' combos like with {{IconSAP|Camel}} or {{IconSAP|Blowfish}}, Tiger will make these combos up to twice as powerful, while Parrot cannot.

Being one of the pets with the most synergies in the entire game, there's a whole lot of tiger combos. It's usually put behind pets with strong combat abilities, but there are plenty of different ways to utilize Tiger. Get creative!

Below is some unique interactions that you should know: 

* Tiger will always repeat the ability of whatever that's currently in front, even when it moves out of its original position. This is useful for Custom packs utilizing pets like {{IconSAP|Panda}}, {{IconSAP|Sword Fish}}, or packs with {{IconSAP|Onion}}.
* It doesn't necessarily ALWAYS make the friend ahead stronger. Since the ability is ''repeated'' at the same level as the Tiger, for certain abilities like {{IconSAP|Crab}} or {{IconSAP|Butterfly}}, a low level Tiger will make them perform their copy abilities again at lower level, and end up copying less stats.

Formerly, if you used tiger on something like {{IconSAP|Egyptian Vulture}}, it could potentially repeat all 3 triggers of the Egyptian Vulture, even at level 1.

==Trivia==
*Tiger is the only pet to have both their appearance and name drastically changed.

The '''Gorilla''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When the Gorilla [[Hurt (Trigger)|is hurt]], it will gain the {{IconSAP|Coconut}} [[Food Perks|perk]], which completely blocks a single instance of damage. However, this ability only triggers a limited number of times per battle. Levelling up the Gorilla increases the amount of times the Coconut perk can be gained.


==Strategy==
With the Custom and Weekly Packs, the Gorilla can be paired with a {{IconSAP|Pepper}}, meaning that it will always trigger its ability, gaining Coconut, guaranteeing that it will be able to attack at least 3 times without dying. This is opposed to giving it {{IconSAP|Melon}}, which runs the risk of the Gorilla not taking damage or taking enough damage that it dies in one hit ({{IconSAP|Salt}}, {{IconSAP|Fortune Cookie}} or {{IconSAP|Sword Fish}}) and therefore not gaining Coconut safely.

If paired with a {{IconSAP|Leech}}, the Gorilla can get permanent Coconut, and still have triggers in the battle.

One fun yet impractical setup is to put a {{IconSAP|Parrot}} behind the Gorilla, and a Leech behind the Parrot. The Parrot will gain permanent Coconut, regardless of if the Leech triggers before the Parrot.

==Trivia==

*Using a Leech, Parrot, Gorilla, and a couple of [[Seagull|Seagulls]], you can get permanent Coconut perk on any pet you want, detailed in this [https://www.reddit.com/r/superautopets/comments/vq4ij1/full_team_of_5050s_with_coconut_armor_in_shop/ reddit post].

The '''Dragon''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack}}'''. Every time a Tier 1 pet is bought, the Dragon scales all pets (excluding the Dragon), up to four times per turn. Leveling up the Dragon will increase the amount of stats it gives to other pets when its ability is triggered. 

==Strategy==
Providing team-wide scaling (excluding itself), Dragon is a strong end-game scaler. Dragon is a solid choice for a pet in teams that do not mind having a free slot open and are looking to scale their 3 other pets.

Dragon's net stat gain per ability proc is +3/+3, +6/+6 and +9/+9 due to the fact you are only buffing 3 pets, as Dragon does not buff itself and you are ideally looking to sell the Tier 1 you bought. Due to this massive stat gain, one will find big value in levelling their Dragon as soon as possible.

Dragon has good synergy with pets that grant you gold or have abilities that work when pets are sold, notable examples being {{IconSAP|Swan}} and {{IconSAP|Buffalo}}. Dragon is very similar to {{IconSAP|Bird of Paradise}}, but it triggers off of buying pets as opposed to spending gold and also will buff your whole, team including the pet you just summoned as opposed to the {{IconSAP|Bird of Paradise}} which only buffs 3 pets. Dragon is more helpful when using a build full of [[Buy-sell Pets]] as opposed to [[Gold Pets]].

It is very hard to trigger Dragon's ability since Dragon is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} pet and the ability will be activated when a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} pet is bought. The dragon can also be seen at {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} when a pet levels up.

==Trivia==
The Dragon is not included in the {{IconSAP|Unicorn Pack}} even though the Dragon is mythical.

The '''Mammoth''' is a [[Tier 6]] [[Pets|Pet]] in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When the Mammoth faints, it gives all of its friends an increased stat boost. Levelling up the Mammoth will increase the stat boost it provides to all friends.

==Strategy==

Mammoth is an incredibly powerful form of in-battle scaling, often capable of catching up and beating opposing scaling boards in {{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}} before they get too far out of reach. Its large starting base stats and strong utility make it a great buff target, and one of the best things to level up into on turn 9. 

Pilling Mammoth should be a fairly rare play unless you have {{IconSAP|Shark}}, since you often lose a lot of stats on the mammoth itself to make that play. Cycling {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} and {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}} can be viable even without shark, especially if you have some form of gold generation or need the stats to survive start of battle snipes!

Mammoth synergizes well with pets and perks that can multiply its effect. With these multipliers you can often gain as many stats as you'd be getting from using a scaler like {{IconSAP|Cat}} or {{IconSAP|Dragon}}. In Turtle Pack, these multipliers include:

- {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} - Doesn't take up any extra board space to double the Mammoth's effect! Can be exploited to get additional triggers on hurt pets or snake.

- {{IconSAP|Whale}} - Fastest way to get Mammoth buffs, arguably Whale's best partner! 

- {{IconSAP|Tiger}} - Unlike Whale and Parrot, Tiger can fully double the effect of a Mushroom'd Mammoth. At level 2 Tiger-Mammoth can potentially give +16/16 to all pets, but make sure to keep the Tiger safe from snipes!

- {{IconSAP|Parrot}} - Probably Mammoth's weakest and slowest multiplier, but can be a great option if you have a level 2 Parrot already! 



==Trivia==

Mammoth and {{IconSAP|Dodo}} are only the Ice Age pets in the {{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}.

The '''Cat''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When Cat is on the team, stat effects from [[Food]] such as {{IconSAP|Pear}} and {{IconSAP|Sushi}} will be multiplied up to two times per turn. This multiplication amount will increase when the Cat is leveled up.

Each level 1 Cat will increase stat effects by 100%, level 2 by 200%, and level 3 by 300%. For example, if there are a level 1 Cat and a level 3 Cat on the team, stat effects will be increased by 400%, and buying an {{IconSAP|Apple}} to one pet will give it 1 + 1*400% = +5 attack and +5 health.

Cat will also affect foods that decrease stats such as {{IconSAP|Broccoli}}. With one level 1 Cat, buying a Broccoli will give -2 attack and +6 health.

Cat does not affect {{IconSAP|Chocolate}} and food perks. For example, it will not increase the extra damage granted from a {{IconSAP|Meat Bone}} food perk.

==Strategy ==
Cat is a late game scalers that can fit into almost any team. By the time Cat becomes available, your team will most likely be set in stone and all there's left to do is buying foods and leveling up, in which case Cat will make each food more powerful and push the team over the finish line.

It's best hunting for high value foods such as {{IconSAP|Pear}}, {{IconSAP|Sushi}}, and {{IconSAP|Pizza}} to gain the most out of Cat's ability. Due to this, Cat's best enablers are actually gold generators like {{IconSAP|Swan}} that will assist greatly in the food search, or pets that directly put foods into the shop such as {{IconSAP|Worm}} and {{IconSAP|Cow}}. Cat Cow is an evergreen combo since each Cow is at minimum +4/+8 to the team due to the Cats multiplication of its {{IconSAP|Milk}}.

One niche strategy with Cat beside scaling the team is using {{IconSAP|Canned Food}} to scale the shop instead. This can be an unexpected combo with potential to be very strong, but extremely hard to pull off.

The '''Snake''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When the nearest friend ahead of the Snake attacks, it will damage a random enemy. Leveling up the Snake will increase the amount of damage it deals. 

==Strategy==
Snake is a high damaging sniper that wants the nearest "space" ahead to attack as many times as possible, and can fit easily in scaling teams behind a friend with high stats, or in summon teams where it will trigger multiple times with the summoned pets. Depending on where the snipes hit, Snake can provide additional damage to finish off powerful frontline enemies, or knocks out weak summoners and backline pets such as {{IconSAP|Turkey}} and {{IconSAP|Shark}}.

Because the ability relies completely on the friend ahead, Snake doesn't require stats and can provide benefits immediately when put on the team. Although not having stats means it can be easily knocked out by other snipers, and since it's often put in second position, it can also be countered with {{IconSAP|Chili}}.

Snake is often paired with {{IconSAP|Tiger}} to double the amount of snipes per attack, and {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} as protection against snipes. Mushroom also fits in nicely in summon teams and especially with {{IconSAP|Fly}}: When Snake faints, it will be resummoned behind the Zombie Fly, adding some additional damage.

The '''Snake''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. When the nearest friend ahead of the Snake attacks, it will damage a random enemy. Leveling up the Snake will increase the amount of damage it deals. 

==Strategy==
Snake is a high damaging sniper that wants the nearest "space" ahead to attack as many times as possible, and can fit easily in scaling teams behind a friend with high stats, or in summon teams where it will trigger multiple times with the summoned pets. Depending on where the snipes hit, Snake can provide additional damage to finish off powerful frontline enemies, or knocks out weak summoners and backline pets such as {{IconSAP|Turkey}} and {{IconSAP|Shark}}.

Because the ability relies completely on the friend ahead, Snake doesn't require stats and can provide benefits immediately when put on the team. Although not having stats means it can be easily knocked out by other snipers, and since it's often put in second position, it can also be countered with {{IconSAP|Chili}}.

Snake is often paired with {{IconSAP|Tiger}} to double the amount of snipes per attack, and {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} as protection against snipes. Mushroom also fits in nicely in summon teams and especially with {{IconSAP|Fly}}: When Snake faints, it will be resummoned behind the Zombie Fly, adding some additional damage.

The '''Fly''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Pets|Pet]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack|image=Turtle Icon.png}}'''. When a friend faints, it will summon a {{IconSAP|Zombie Fly}} where that pet fainted. This ability can only activate 3 times per turn. Levelling up the Fly increases the stats and level of the summoned Zombie Fly

Fly's ability will not trigger until there are spaces for the Zombie Flies to spawn in. When used with other Faint abilities such as {{IconSAP|Rooster}} or {{IconSAP|Deer}}, it will "wait" until the tokens have been cleared before summoning Zombie Flies.

When a Zombie Fly faints, it will not trigger Fly's ability.

==Strategy==
Fly is a good value buy since it's almost guaranteed to give 3 summons, something that other summoners can accidentally waste by running out of space. It can be thought of as 3 gold for a 16/16, and can sometimes be used just for the pure stats it can provide.

Fly pairs well with summoning pets such as {{IconSAP|Turkey}} as well as {{IconSAP|Shark}}, since one Fly is equal to 4 faint triggers in battle. It also combos nicely with {{IconSAP|Snake}}: whatever that's in front of Snake will turn into a Zombie Fly after fainting and give Snake an extra snipe. Fly tends to be positioned at the last 2 spaces to make sure enough faints occur for it to use up all of its triggers, which often makes it vulnerable to {{IconSAP|Crocodile}}.

===Custom packs===
A niche synergy the Fly has is with Faint Scaling teams ({{IconSAP|Shark}}, {{IconSAP|Praying Mantis}} and {{IconSAP|Spinosaurus}}), in which it will summon a Zombie Fly that can be sold for 1, 2 or 3 gold (depending on level) everytime a friendly pet faints in the shop from a {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill}} or the Praying Mantis' ability.

The '''Apple''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''', the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Golden Pack}}'''. When a pet is fed an Apple, it receives +1 attack and +1 health. The {{IconSAP|Pear}}, {{IconSAP|Lasagna}} and {{IconSAP|Chicken Leg}} are generally considered to be direct upgrades to it.

The {{IconSAP|Mouse}} and {{IconSAP|Worm}} will stock an Apple when sold/at the start of turn, at level 2 they will stock a {{IconSAP|Better Apple|nolink=yes}} and at level 3 they will stock a {{IconSAP|Best Apple|nolink=yes}} that give +2/+2 and +3/+3 respectively.
==Strategy==
Generally, the Apple is worth the 3 {{IconSAP|Gold}} cost during the early rounds since the stat boost is often what dictates a win, especially if it is being fed to a Pet that you plan to have stick around for a while and you do not want or need to buy many Pets from the shop. 

Can be stocked for free by a Mouse when sold and for 2 gold by a {{IconSAP|Worm}} at the start of turn.

If {{IconSAP|Jerboa}} is in the pack, it is beneficial for the Apples to be especially looked out for so the Jerboa can buff the rest of your Pets.

==Trivia==
*The Apple is one of only 3 foods to have the "Better" and "Best" upgrades to it, the others being {{IconSAP|Chocolate}} and {{IconSAP|Milk}}.

The '''Honey''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Food]], available in  the'''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Feeding a [[Pets|pet]] Honey will give it the Honey [[Food Perks|perk]]. When a pet with Honey perk faints, it summons a level 1 {{IconSAP|Bee}} in its place.

== Strategy ==
The Honey can be placed on pets in front of those who have the Friend ahead attacks ability trigger such as {{IconSAP|Snake}} and {{IconSAP|Kangaroo}} or in teams which benefit from [[Summon Pets]] with abilities such as {{IconSAP|Horse|name=Horse's}} and {{IconSAP|Turkey|name=Turkey's}}. It can also be used in builds with certain [[Faint Pets]] that have abilities like that of the {{IconSAP|Shark|name=Shark's}}.

Whilst the Honey is a somewhat potent food early game, it loses its value quite harshly later on and thus should be swapped for other [[Food Perks]] such as the {{IconSAP|Melon|name=Melon perk}} or the {{IconSAP|Steak|name=Steak perk}}.

Honey can be used as a tiebreaker, as the Bee will spawn after the last 2 Pets fought, allowing you to win.

It is a good early game food, but performs disadvantageously against pets that have the [[Knock Out (Trigger)|Knock Out]] or [[Hurt (Trigger)|Hurt abilities]] (e.g. {{IconSAP|Hippo}}, {{IconSAP|Blowfish}}) as it will give them a safe way to activate their abilities.

The '''Garlic''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Feeding a pet Garlic will give it the Garlic [[Food Perks|perk]]. A pet with Garlic perk will take 2 less damage from all sources, although damage can't be reduced below 2. 

==Strategy==
Garlic is an early game defensive perk that can stay useful until the end of the game. The damage reduction can be crippling against early turn enemies with low attack. Dumping stats onto a single pet then giving it Garlic is a strong strategy that has next to no counters until {{IconSAP|Skunk}} and {{IconSAP|Scorpion}} are available.

Despite falling off in later turns since the damage reduction won't be as substantial, it's still a useful perk even when compared to {{IconSAP|Melon}}. Garlic is still good at reducing repeated chip damage such as {{IconSAP|Blowfish}}, {{IconSAP|Snake}}, or summon teams. Even in end game, it's important to consider that a 50/50 pet with Garlic and a 50/50 with Melon will still trade equally and knock each other out after 2 hits.

'''End turn''': Increase sell value by 1 {{IconSAP|gold}}. }} ''This page details information about the incremental sell value perk. For other cake-related foods, see {{IconSAP|Chocolate Cake}} or {{IconSAP|Eat-Me Cake}}.'' The '''Cake''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 3}} [[Food]], available for free in '''{{IconSAP|Custom Packs}}'''. Feeding a pet the Cake will give them the Cake [[Perk|perk]]. A pet with the Cake perk will increase its sell value by 1 {{IconSAP|gold}} at the end of the turn. ==Strategy== With Cake's availability in the early game, it works well on strong pets you plan on selling later. For example, a Level 2 {{IconSAP|Cricket}} at 3/5 can help your team early in the game but will inevitably need to be sold for a stronger replacement. With Cake, you can use the Cricket as an investment so that a burst of gold is earned once it's finally sold. Beyond '''Turtle Pack''', the sell value buffs synergize with specific pet abilities found in '''{{IconSAP|Custom Packs}}'''. For each gained sell value, {{IconSAP|Trout}} earns more health when that friend is sold. {{FoodInfoBox
|tier=4
|effect=Give one pet the Bread [[Food Perks|perk]]. '''End turn''': Gain +7 {{IconSAP|health|nolink=yes}} until next turn
|image=Bread.png}}

'''Bread''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Feeding a [[Pets|pet]] Bread will give them the Bread [[Food Perks|perk]]. At the end of turn, a pet with the Bread perk will gain +7 {{IconSAP|health|nolink=yes}} until next turn.

== Strategy ==
Bread is a mid-game defensive perk. It works for the usual purposes of extending pets' lifespan, giving them more chances to attack and trigger their abilities. Although, Bread has unique strengths that make it stand out compared to {{IconSAP|Garlic}} and {{IconSAP|Melon}} that can be found earlier.

7 health is ''at least'' 3.5 times the amount of damage Garlic can reduce per hit. Meaning at bare minimum, if the pet isn't gonna be attacked by more than 3 hits, Bread is a direct upgrade to Garlic. It's especially useful against big bursts of damage like from {{IconSAP|Crocodile}}, 7 health is the exact amount needed to escape the 8 damage breakpoint, making it an efficient counter to put on backliners such as {{IconSAP|Shark}} and {{IconSAP|Turkey}}.

The health is gained before battle, making it "immune" to chip damage snipers or ailments from other packs that can break or override perks and disable their defensive capabilities. This also allows for synergies with {{IconSAP|Turtle}} for an effective total of +27 health, or {{IconSAP|Whale}} that will release the pet still with +7 health intact.

Bread should be swapped for other perks as the pet gets scaled closer to 50 health, since it will be entirely useless once it reaches that point.

== Trivia ==
* With Bread's addition in [[Version 0.46]],  '''Turtle Pack''' currently has the most foods out of all the non-custom packs (18 different foods).
* Bread is one of five bread-related foods in '''Super Auto Pets''', the other four being {{IconSAP|Baguette}}, {{IconSAP|Bread Crumbs}}, {{IconSAP|Faint Bread}}, and {{IconSAP|Pita Bread}}.
* Before Bread's removal and reintroduction, Bread was a functionless perk given to the {{IconSAP|Dolphin}}(s) summoned by {{IconSAP|Beluga Sturgeon}}.

}}
'''Canned Food''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack}}'''. When bought, instead of giving stats to pets currently on the team, it gives permanent +1 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}} and +1 {{IconSAP|health|nolink=yes}} to all current ''and future'' shop pets.

== Strategy ==
Canned Food, or simply known as "Can", is a food that supports pivoting. It's an {{IconSAP|Apple}} for any pet that you might put on the team later, even ones that haven't shown up yet such as tier 5 and 6 pets, giving them a head start in scaling. Another way to conceptualize its strength is if the entire team will eventually be replaced by high tier pets, then each Can is 3 gold for +5/+5. It pairs well with pivot pets such as {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, {{IconSAP|Lobster}}, and {{IconSAP|Chicken}}.

Since the buffs can accumulate, buying more Cans will make the shop bigger and bigger. The effect works with {{IconSAP|Cat}}'s ability, making Cat Can a hard to pull off, but extremely rewarding strategy that can max out the stats of all shop pets.

==Trivia==
*The Canned Food is the first food to affect Shop pets.

The '''Pear''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 4}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Feeding a [[Pets|Pet]] a Pear increases its stats by +2 attack and +2 health permanently. 

Essentially, it's a better {{IconSAP|Apple}} but a worse {{IconSAP|Lasagna}}/{{IconSAP|Chicken Leg}}.

There isn't a lot to be said, feed it to pets when appropriate and generally try to avoid feeding it to pets you don't intend to keep for long. The {{IconSAP|Seal}} and {{IconSAP|Rabbit}} create more stats from feeding pets food and Pears are a solid option to trigger those effects. The Pear's stats can also be multiplied by a {{IconSAP|Cat}}.

'''Chili''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Feeding a [[Pets|pet]] a Chili will give that pet the Chili [[Food Perks|perk]]. Every time a pet with Chili perk attacks, it will deal an additional 5 damage to the pet in second space of the enemy's team. If there are no enemies in that space, Chili will not deal damage.

== Strategy ==
Chili acts as chip damage to pets behind the main target. It is useful for countering second position supporters such as {{IconSAP|Snake}} or {{IconSAP|Tiger}}, breaking backline {{IconSAP|Melon}} perks before they become a threat once they're in front, and especially useful against summoners such as {{IconSAP|Rooster}} or {{IconSAP|Fly}} to sweep all the high attack but low health tokens.

When paired with {{IconSAP|Panther}}, Chili becomes even scarier with 2x/3x/4x damage to the second enemy. A level 3 Panther with Chili will deal ''20 damage'' to the second enemy.

The '''Chocolate''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 5}} [[Food]] that can be found in '''Any''' pack. When Chocolate is given to a [[Pets|pet]], it will receive +1 {{IconSAP|experience|nolink=yes}}. Similar to when combining duplicate copies, each Chocolate/experience will also add +1 {{IconSAP|attack|nolink=yes}} and +1 {{IconSAP|health|nolink=yes}}.

In Custom and Weekly pack, {{IconSAP|Crow}} can stock Chocolate upon being sold, and at higher levels will stock {{IconSAP|Better Chocolate|nolink=yes}} and {{IconSAP|Best Chocolate|nolink=yes}} that give +2 and +3 experiences respectively.

== Strategy ==
Each Chocolate represents a "wild card" duplicate that can be used to level up any pet faster. Almost every pet benefits from leveling up, so Chocolate brings consistency to every team, and it becomes available right when the pet pool becomes big enough that it can be difficult to find the exact duplicate that you need. Due to just how useful Chocolate is, it can often be a good idea not to freeze other foods starting from turn 8 (going into shop tier 5), just to increase the odds of finding more Chocolates.

Generally speaking, if there are duplicate copies in the shop and Chocolate, the duplicates should be bought first, since Chocolate can be used on any pet while the copies can only be combined on specific pets.

==Trivia==
* As of the Golden Pack update ([[Version 0.24]]), every [[Weekly Pack]] now contains Chocolate.

The '''Steak''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack}}'''. Feed a [[Pets|pet]] a Steak wil give that pet the Steak [[Food Perks|perk]]. The first time a pet with Steak perk attacks, it will deal an additional 20 damage.

==Strategy==
Steak can be thought of as the inverse of {{IconSAP|Melon}}. While Melon is often the more flexible choice that can fit on almost any team since surviving longer will give the pet more chances to attack and activating their abilities. Steak instead fills the niche of eliminating the enemies faster and denying them from activating ''their'' abilities. Against pets that benefit from attacking multiple times such as {{IconSAP|Elephant}} or {{IconSAP|Snake}} combos, it's best to knock them out as soon as possible instead of trading over multiple strikes.

It's often great value to put Steak on pets with low stats that benefit little from the additional survivability that Garlic and Melon can provide. Additionally, since Turtle pack teams tend to have more health than attack, Steak can prove to be more useful than Melon when put on the lobsided 25/50 pets.

{{FoodInfoBox
|image=Melon.png
|tier=6
|effect=Give one pet the Melon [[Food Perks|perk]]. Take 20 less {{IconSAP|damage|nolink=yes}}, once.
}}
The '''Melon''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack}}'''. Feeding a [[Pets|Pet]] a Melon gives that pet the Melon [[Food Perks|perk]]. The first time a pet with Melon perk takes damage, the damage is reduced by 20, to a minimum of 0.

==Strategy==
Melon is a very efficient defensive perk that's used to keep your pets alive longer. If you're not looking for synergy perks like {{IconSAP|Mushroom}}, it's always good to give your pets Melon. 

It can be considered a whopping ''20 health'' food that can exceed the 50 health limit. More health also means more times the pet gets to attack and the more chances it have to trigger its ability. A 35/31 pet with Melon perk can go toe-to-toe against a max stat enemy at 50/50 with common defensive food perks. Melon can also protect your pets against high damaging snipers like {{IconSAP|Leopard}}, or against instant knockouts by {{IconSAP|Scorpion}}.

On the other hand, it also shouldn't be treated as a stronger version of {{IconSAP|Garlic}} or {{IconSAP|Bread}}, as they all have their unique strengths and weaknesses. Melon only blocks damage once so has way too many counters such as: putting a disposable pet front-most to act as a meatshield that breaks the Melon, snipes or piercing abilities like {{IconSAP|Chili}} or {{IconSAP|Rhino}} that break it before the pet gets to attack, summon teams that can afford to waste a token on the Melon then swarm the exposed pet, and so on. Reducing the damage to 0 might not always be ideal, since you can lose out on Hurt triggers from pets like {{IconSAP|Camel}} or {{IconSAP|Gorilla}}.

==Trivia==

*In the early days of Super Auto Pets Melon was instead called a shield and, ignoring visual differences, functioned almost identically to the Melon we have today.
The upgrade of the Melon is the {{IconSAP|Coconut}} but abilities and attack takes infinite damage. The downgrade of the Melon is the {{IconSAP|Lemon}} or {{IconSAP|Garlic}}

|tier=6

}}

'''Mushroom''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 6}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}'''. Feeding a [[Pets|pet]] a Mushroom gives that pet the Mushroom [[Food Perks|perk]]. When a pet with the Mushroom perk faints, it summons a 1/1 copy of itself at the same level.

Summoned copies are considered "new" pets, with almost no memory of their old selves before they faint. For example if a {{IconSAP|Parrot}} faints and comes back, it will not keep the copied abilities. However, Mushroom ''does'' remember the amount of ability triggers the pet has spent.

== Strategy ==
Mushroom's biggest strength is giving pets an additional, guaranteed chance to trigger their abilities. Some examples include the {{IconSAP|Elephant}}, {{IconSAP|Turtle}}, {{IconSAP|Deer}}, {{IconSAP|Mammoth}}. It combines well with {{IconSAP|Scorpion}}, enabling it to break {{IconSAP|Melon}} on its first attack, then respawn with {{IconSAP|Peanut}} and knock out the exposed enemy.

It can also be used as a defensive perk for support pets that don't care much about their own stats, such as {{IconSAP|Turkey}}, {{IconSAP|Tiger}}, {{IconSAP|Snake}}. Mushroom on these pets is as strong if not stronger than {{IconSAP|Bread}} and {{IconSAP|Melon}}, since the pet is guaranteed to survive any Start of battle snipers.

==Trivia==
* The '''Mushroom''' effect can be a reference to [https://wikipedia.org/Super_Mario Super Mario]'s [https://www.mariowiki.com/1-Up_Mushroom 1-Up Mushroom].

The '''Apple''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} [[Food]], available in the '''{{IconSAP|Turtle Pack}}''', the '''{{IconSAP|Puppy Pack}}''' and the '''{{IconSAP|Golden Pack}}'''. When a pet is fed an Apple, it receives +1 attack and +1 health. The {{IconSAP|Pear}}, {{IconSAP|Lasagna}} and {{IconSAP|Chicken Leg}} are generally considered to be direct upgrades to it.

The {{IconSAP|Mouse}} and {{IconSAP|Worm}} will stock an Apple when sold/at the start of turn, at level 2 they will stock a {{IconSAP|Better Apple|nolink=yes}} and at level 3 they will stock a {{IconSAP|Best Apple|nolink=yes}} that give +2/+2 and +3/+3 respectively.
==Strategy==
Generally, the Apple is worth the 3 {{IconSAP|Gold}} cost during the early rounds since the stat boost is often what dictates a win, especially if it is being fed to a Pet that you plan to have stick around for a while and you do not want or need to buy many Pets from the shop. 

Can be stocked for free by a Mouse when sold and for 2 gold by a {{IconSAP|Worm}} at the start of turn.

If {{IconSAP|Jerboa}} is in the pack, it is beneficial for the Apples to be especially looked out for so the Jerboa can buff the rest of your Pets.

==Trivia==
*The Apple is one of only 3 foods to have the "Better" and "Best" upgrades to it, the others being {{IconSAP|Chocolate}} and {{IconSAP|Milk}}.

The '''Ram''' is a [[Tokens|Token]] [[Pets|Pet]] with no abilities. Up to two of them spawn (depending on available slots) when a {{IconSAP|Sheep}} faints. As with all tokens, it is considered a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} for the sake of certain abilities like {{IconSAP|Poodle|name=Poodle's}} and {{IconSAP|Rhino|name=Rhino's}}. The Ram's starting stats increase depending on the level of the {{IconSAP|Sheep}} that summoned them.

== Strategy ==
An easy way to get the hidden sticker [[Achievements|Achievement]] for  the Ram is to level a Sheep to Level 2 and then use a [[Sleeping Pill]] on the Sheep while having an empty slot available. This will spawn two Level 2 Rams into the user's team which can then be combined into a single Level 3 Ram.  This is also particularly useful when trying to acquire a quick Level 3 Pet to activate the [[Bison|Bison's]] ability. As with all tokens, it is considered a {{IconSAP|Tier 1}} for the sake of certain abilities like {{IconSAP|Poodle|name=Poodle's}} and {{IconSAP|Rhino|name=Rhino's}}.

The '''Peanut''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 7}} [[Food Perks|Perk]], not normally available in the shop and only capable of being obtained through abilities. Whenever a pet with the Peanut perk attacks and hurts an enemy, the enemy will be instantly knocked out.

== Strategy ==
Peanut acts as a special counter against scalers. Once hurt, regardless of how beefy the enemies are, they will be instantly knocked out by Peanut.

The pet with Peanut perk only really has to care about health. The longer it survives, the more likely it is to knock out more enemies. However, the enemy needs to be considered "hurt" in order to be knocked out. So against {{IconSAP|Melon}}, the pet with Peanut needs to have 21 attack or higher to break through the Melon and knock them out. Peanut will always lose against {{IconSAP|Coconut}}.

An ideal Peanut pet stays at 21 attack, and does not need to be scaled any further. The more stats it receives, the less effective Peanut is. At certain point, it won't be any more useful than other food perks.

A special interaction is against 1 health enemies with {{IconSAP|Pepper}}. The pepper will keep the enemy at 1 health, so they will receive 0 damage and won't be knocked out by Peanut.

==Obtaining Peanut==

{{IconSAP|Scorpion}} comes with Peanut and is the most common Peanut pet.

{{IconSAP|Terror Bird}} gives out Peanuts to friends with the {{IconSAP|Strawberry}} perk, but only at start of battle.

==Trivia==
Peanut is one of only three foods or pets in the game to be classified as {{IconSAP|Tier 7}}, alongside {{IconSAP|Peanut Butter}} and {{IconSAP|Coconut}}. Long considered by the community to be Tier 7 perks because of their extremely powerful nature that far exceeded the abilities of comparable Tier 6 perks like {{IconSAP|Steak}} or {{IconSAP|Melon}}, they were officially moved to a new tier in [[Version 0.41|Update 0.41]] (largely because of the ease of obtaining them with {{IconSAP|Cardinal}}). If you hover over Peanut, it will show a die with 7 dots, exceeding the maximum possible to reach via the shop and in fact the maximum possible on a normal 6-sided die.

|image=Coconut.png
|tier=7
|effect=Block damage, once.}}

The '''Coconut''' is a {{IconSAP|Tier 7}} [[Food]], but isn't normally available in the shop and can only be obtained through abilities. The first time a pet with the Coconut perk takes damage, the damage is reduced to 0.

==Strategy==
Blocking all damage makes it a hard counter to {{IconSAP|Peanut}} and {{IconSAP|Peanut Butter}} perks, as well as allowing pets to survive high burst of damage regardless of their health. However it's not always better than the more readily available {{IconSAP|Melon}}, since Coconut cannot trigger Hurt abilities.

For example: When a 50/50 {{IconSAP|Gorilla}} with Coconut goes up against another 50/50 enemy with any defensive food perk, they will knock each other out after 2 hits. However if the Gorilla had had Melon or {{IconSAP|Garlic}} instead, it would've knocked the other 50/50 out in 2 hits, but gained Coconut after the first hit, survived, and could get a 3rd hit in against the second enemy.

==Obtaining Coconut outside battle==
Hurting a {{IconSAP|Gorilla}} in the shop phase will trigger its ability and give it permanent Coconut. This can be done by {{IconSAP|Sleeping Pill|name=Pilling}} a {{IconSAP|Hedgehog}} or {{IconSAP|Badger}}.

In Custom and Weekly packs, {{IconSAP|Coconut Crab}} can be used in the shop phase to gain a temporary Coconut. In order to give permanent Coconut to any pet or potentially the entire team, we'll need to create a Custom pack and follow these steps:

====Step 1: Parrot====
'''Goal''': At the end of turn, let a {{IconSAP|Parrot}} copy Gorilla's ability, then hurt the Parrot to trigger the copied ability and give itself Coconut.

This can be done by putting a {{IconSAP|Leech}} behind the Parrot, or with {{IconSAP|Deer Lord}} behind a Hedgehog or Badger. Remember that Parrot's copy ability has to go first, so make sure Leech/Deer Lord has lower attack than Parrot.

====Step 2: Transfer====
'''Goal''': At the end of turn, let the Parrot with Coconut copy a {{IconSAP|Seagull}}, faint a {{IconSAP|Chipmunk}} or {{IconSAP|Toucan}} or Seagull that has {{IconSAP|Mushroom}} perk, when that pet respawns, the Parrot will give it Coconut. Once Coconut is on one of these 3 pets, it can easily be copied to other pets on the team.

An example setup would be: Leech, Seagull with Mushroom, Parrot with Coconut, Seagull. The Seagull in front of the Parrot should not have any food perk, or has run out of triggers already.

Now, we need the Leech to knock out the Seagull in front. This can be guaranteed by putting that it at 1 health: by letting it get hurt by the Leech prior to this turn, feeding it {{IconSAP|Fried Shrimp}} or {{IconSAP|Eat-Me Cake}}, or giving it a Mushroom then Sleeping Pill so it will respawn as 1/1. Alternatively, putting {{IconSAP|Pineapple}} or {{IconSAP|Kiwano}} on the Leech will allow it to knock out a base stats Seagull immediately.

====Step 3: Chipmunk====
'''Goal''': Stock Coconuts in the shop with Chipmunk. Now we can fully pivot to any pets of our choosing and give them Coconut.

Congratulations! Hopefully that takes less than 20 turns, enjoy the full Coconut team!
